```text
1006	/**
1007	 * Append a single worker entry to the JSONL file. The writer assigns
1008	 * `seq` from the in-memory cursor (seeded from the file tail on first
1009	 * use). Acquires the per-worker chain so it cannot interleave with
1010	 * compaction/expand/delete.
1011	 *
1012	 * If `entry.id` is already present on disk (or in the seen-ids cache),
1013	 * the call is a no-op and the previously persisted entry is returned
1014	 * with `appended: false` so wake-up publishers do not re-announce old seqs.
1015	 */
1016	export type AppendWorkerEntryResult = {
1017	  entry: WorkerEntry;
1018	  appended: boolean;
1019	};
1020	
1021	export async function appendWorkerEntryWithResult(
1022	  runId: string,
1023	  workerId: string,
1024	  entry: Omit<WorkerEntry, "seq">,
1025	): Promise<AppendWorkerEntryResult> {
1026	  return runOnChain(runId, workerId, async () => {
1027	    return withWorkerFileLock(runId, workerId, async (paths) => {
1028	      // If a compaction race somehow stranded the plaintext file under .gz,
1029	      // expand it first so cache refresh sees the live transcript rather
1030	      // than the lock-created empty placeholder.
1031	      await expandWorkerOutputFileInternal(paths);
1032	      // Never resume numbering above a head that isn't on disk.
1033	      await healStrandedStreamHead(runId, workerId, paths);
1034	
1035	      const { nextSeq, seen, fingerprints } = await refreshChainCaches(runId, workerId);
1036	      if (entry.id && seen.has(entry.id)) {
1037	        // Already persisted; load it back so the caller has a stable
1038	        // record. Linear scan is fine: this is the dedup path and runs at
1039	        // append cadence, not read cadence.
1040	        const persisted = await readCanonicalPersistedEntries(runId, workerId);
1041	        const match = persisted.find((line) => line.id === entry.id);
1042	        if (match && typeof match.seq === "number") {
1043	          return { entry: match, appended: false };
1044	        }
1045	        // Legacy line without seq: assign one virtually based on file
1046	        // position. The writer doesn't advance nextSeq in this case.
1047	        return { entry: { ...(entry as WorkerEntry), seq: 0 }, appended: false };
1048	      }
1049	
1050	      const persistedEntry: WorkerEntry = {
1051	        ...(entry as WorkerEntry),
1052	        seq: nextSeq,
1053	      };
1054	      const compact = compactEntryForHistory(persistedEntry as unknown as CompactableEntry) as unknown as WorkerEntry;
1055	      const line = JSON.stringify(compact) + "\n";
1056	
1057	      const target = paths.filePath;
1058	      const newlineGuard = await needsLeadingNewline(target);
1059	      // Capture pre-append size so we can record the byte offset of the
1060	      // new line in the sparse seq→offset index. The newline-guard byte
1061	      // (if any) is written before the JSON line, so the line starts one
1062	      // byte past sizeBefore in that case.
1063	      let sizeBefore = 0;
1064	      try {
1065	        sizeBefore = (await fs.stat(target)).size;
1066	      } catch (error) {
1067	        if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") throw error;
1068	      }
1069	      const lineStartOffset = sizeBefore + (newlineGuard ? 1 : 0);
1070	      const handle = await fs.open(target, "a");
1071	      try {
1072	        await handle.appendFile(newlineGuard ? "\n" + line : line, "utf8");
1073	        await handle.sync();
1074	      } finally {
1075	        await handle.close();
1076	      }
1077	
1078	      if (shouldIndex(persistedEntry.seq)) {
1079	        // Best-effort: appendIndexEntry swallows its own errors. The
1080	        // index is opportunistic — a failure here only slows future tail
1081	        // reads until the next rebuild.
1082	        await appendIndexEntry(target, {
1083	          seq: persistedEntry.seq,
1084	          offset: lineStartOffset,
1085	        });
1086	      }
1087	
1088	      if (entry.id) {
1089	        seen.add(entry.id);
1090	        fingerprints.set(entry.id, workerEntryFingerprint(compact));
1091	      }
1092	      nextSeqByKey.set(chainKey(runId, workerId), nextSeq + 1);
1093	      await rememberWorkerFileState(runId, workerId);
1094	      const { commitArtifactAppend } = await import("@/server/artifacts/stream-metadata");
1095	      await commitArtifactAppend({
1096	        streamId: { runId, kind: "worker_entries", ownerId: workerId },
1097	        seq: compact.seq,
1098	        recordId: compact.id ?? `seq-${compact.seq}`,
1099	      });
1100	      return { entry: compact, appended: true };
1101	    });
1102	  });
1103	}
1104	
1105	export async function appendWorkerEntry(
1106	  runId: string,
1107	  workerId: string,
1108	  entry: Omit<WorkerEntry, "seq">,
1109	): Promise<WorkerEntry> {
1110	  return (await appendWorkerEntryWithResult(runId, workerId, entry)).entry;

1113	/**
1114	 * Diff-and-append a batch of bridge-emitted output entries. Exact
1115	 * replays are skipped, but changed records with the same bridge id are
1116	 * appended as revisions. Streaming assistant prose can arrive first as
1117	 * "One" and later as the complete paragraph; the append-only stream must
1118	 * publish that later revision with a fresh seq so clients repaint.
1119	 *
1120	 * Existing callers (`persistWorkerSnapshot`) get the same observable
1121	 * behavior as the old overwrite-on-snapshot path with no file rewrite.
1122	 */
1123	export async function writeWorkerOutputEntries(
1124	  runId: string,
1125	  workerId: string,
1126	  entries: AgentRecord["outputEntries"],
1127	) {
1128	  if (!Array.isArray(entries) || entries.length === 0) {
1129	    return;
1130	  }
1131	
1132	  await runOnChain(runId, workerId, async () => {
1133	    await withWorkerFileLock(runId, workerId, async (paths) => {
1134	      await expandWorkerOutputFileInternal(paths);
1135	      // Never resume numbering above a head that isn't on disk.
1136	      await healStrandedStreamHead(runId, workerId, paths);
1137	
1138	      const { fingerprints } = await refreshChainCaches(runId, workerId);
1139	      const newEntries: AgentOutputEntry[] = [];
1140	      const acceptedFingerprintsById = new Map<string, string>();
1141	      for (const entry of entries) {
1142	        if (!entry) continue;
1143	        // The agent-runtime live view prepends a synthetic archive marker
1144	        // ("X older raw worker activity records are only in archived
1145	        // history…") when entries have been pruned past the live window.
1146	        // It is a render-time hint, not real conversation content — never
1147	        // persist it into the unified worker stream.
1148	        if (entry.id === "output-archive-marker") {
1149	          continue;
1150	        }
1151	        // Real bridge entries always carry an id; tooling/migration code that
1152	        // hands us synthetic snapshots may not. In that case, treat the entry
1153	        // as opaque and always append (no dedup possible).
1154	        //
1155	        // Dedup keyed on (id, fingerprint): re-writing the exact same
1156	        // entry is a no-op, but a streaming chunk that grew between two
1157	        // persistWorkerSnapshot calls produces a second row with the
1158	        // same id and a longer text — the FE is expected to coalesce by
1159	        // id and render the latest revision. (Test:
```

## The turn you read did finish; a queued message immediately started a new one

| id | action | queued at | status |

| `f2f1e4ca` — "update the user avatar… upload picture, check dimensions…" | `queue` | **13:39:55** | **`delivering`** ⏳ |

At **13:44:37** the worker finished the steer turn (`direct_worker_awaiting_user`, reason `worker_requested_input`) — that's the completed answer you're looking at, ending with "Want me to drive the editor at 390px and screenshot it?". In the same second, the queue drain saw `workerStatus: idle`, decided `drain`, and shipped `f2f1e4ca` into a brand-new turn.

It's alive and mid-flight right now — the stream is still appending:

```
.omniharness/agent-runtime-output/a7d6c9fab3bb-worker-1.jsonl   (modified 13:47:36)
```

That's your avatar-upload task, ~3 minutes in.

This is the real complaint, and it's a genuine UX gap. In the background-drain path, the user's message is only written to the worker stream **after** `askAgent` returns:

The tradeoff in that comment is real — pre-appending would show phantom messages on a retry loop — but "working with no visible prompt" is the worse failure mode. A pending/optimistic entry that's reconciled or dropped on failure would fix it, and per `docs/architecture/worker-conversation-stream.md` it belongs in the unified stream rather than a sidecar.

The user is pointing out that not only is the queued message missing from the UI, but the worker's live output for the new turn isn't displaying either—the last visible content is from the previous turn. The critical question is whether the JSONL file being written to is the same one the UI is reading from.

I'm realizing there's a path mismatch: the raw agent runtime output is going to `.omniharness/agent-runtime-output/a7d6c9fab3bb-worker-1.jsonl`, but according to AGENTS.md, the unified worker stream that the UI actually renders should be at `app-data/run-data/<runId>/<workerId>.jsonl`. When I checked earlier, that directory didn't exist—the ls command failed. That's a major red flag. Additionally, I noticed that `worker.output_entries_json` is empty and `current_text` is blank, while `last_text` still contains the previous turn's content. During an active turn with live streaming, `current_text` should be updating, so the fact that it's empty is suspicious.

Looking at the timestamps, `updated_at = 1785843877` (13:44:37) and nothing has changed since—over 3 minutes have passed despite the agent actively streaming. This tells me the live sync isn't persisting streaming deltas for this turn. The issue is that in direct-mode drain, `askAgent` is awaited, meaning the turn is driven by the drain loop rather than the live worker sync path. And `persistDeliveredWorkerResponse` only gets called after `askAgent` returns, so the entire turn's output gets buffered and written to the unified stream all at once at the end. Both the user prompt and worker output are deferred—nothing streams live. That's why the UI just shows a spinner for the whole turn with no output appearing.

But there might be a separate live streaming path for direct control messages. When you type directly, the worker does stream live with `current_text` updating. There's probably a live sync loop that reads agent snapshots and appends deltas. The key question is whether `runWorkerTurn` creates a per-worker turn gate that blocks the live sync from acquiring it during the drain's `askAgent` call—if so, that would explain why zero updates appear.

I need to check the sync implementation and output store to see if app-data/run-data exists, and run several diagnostic checks in parallel. The user is clearly frustrated, so I should be efficient about finding the root cause and then offer to fix it rather than just diagnose.

## Claude · 2026-08-04T11:58:01.563Z

Server's healthy — other runs ticked at 13:55:50. Only `a7d6c9fab3bb` is frozen. Here's the real cause; my last answer was wrong about it being fine.

## The agent is blocked asking you a question that was never rendered

At **13:47:55** the worker raised an elicitation and stopped:

```json
{"type":"elicitation","status":"pending",
 "text":"Question for user: Please answer the following questions. (3 fields)",
 "raw":{"toolCallId":"toolu_017VYct8YVQXoQEPpAQsaLN1","requestedSchema":{...}}}
```

It's a 3-field AskUserQuestion about the avatar work — "Google profile pictures aren't captured today. Should I fix that as part of this?", "How should the square framing work?", and a third. It's been parked on that for ~10 minutes. The ACP process is still alive; it's waiting on you.

## Why you can't see it — and can't answer it

The turn is being driven by the background queue drain, which buffers **everything** until `askAgent()` returns (`src/server/conversations/queued-messages.ts`):

```ts
1337  const response = await askAgent(workerId, workerPromptForRun(run, workerContent));  // ← blocked forever
1340  await appendUserInputOnDelivery({ ... });        // never reached
1353  await db.insert(messages).values(userMessage);   // never reached
1354  await persistDeliveredWorkerResponse({ ... });   // never reached
```

`askAgent` can't return until the elicitation is answered. Nothing after it runs. So the entire turn — your prompt, every token of output, and the question itself — has never been written to the unified worker stream the UI renders from.

That's literal, not theoretical:

```
.omniharness/run-data/a7d6c9fab3bb/          ← does not exist
find .omniharness/run-data -name "*worker*.jsonl" | wc -l   →  818   (for other runs)
```

818 worker stream files on disk, **zero** for this run. Corroborated everywhere:

| signal | value |
|---|---|
| `workers.status` | `working`, frozen at 13:44:37 |
| `workers.current_text` | length **0** |
| `workers.output_entries_json` | `[]` |
| `execution_events` after 13:44:37 | **0** |
| `clarifications` rows | **0** |
| `f2f1e4ca` queue row | `delivering`, `delivered_at` NULL |

So the deadlock closes on itself: **you can't answer the question because it was never surfaced, and it can't be surfaced because surfacing only happens after it's answered.** Everything you'd need to see is sitting in `.omniharness/agent-runtime-output/` — which is the raw ACP log, not a UI source.

The code comment right above this block names this exact failure:

`queued-messages.ts:1245-1248`
```
// A pending elicitation belongs to the turn that is already running. Do
// not queue its answer behind that same turn: the turn cannot finish until
// the answer arrives, so acquiring the per-worker turn gate here creates a
// self-deadlock and leaves the queue row in `delivering` forever.
```

The guard it protects (line 1249) only checks for an elicitation pending **before** the drain starts. This one was raised **during** the drained turn, so it walks straight past — same deadlock, other door.

## Recovery options

There's a designed escape hatch at lines 1249-1287: a *newly queued* message is checked against a pending elicitation and answered directly, **without** taking the turn gate. Sending a message into the session now would likely hit that path — the `queue_drain_decision` events stopped simply because `pendingCount` went to 0, not because sync died, so the drain loop should still pick up a new `pending` row.

Two caveats I can't resolve without trying it: the answer is fed as free text into a structured 3-field `oneOf` schema, so the mapping may be junk; and `f2f1e4ca` will stay wedged in `delivering` regardless. The safe alternative is stopping/interrupting the worker and re-sending the avatar request, losing the ~3 minutes of work.

I haven't touched anything. Want me to:
- **try the recovery** — send an answer into the session and watch whether the elicitation path picks it up, or
- **fix the bug** — surface elicitations raised mid-drain (append the user input and stream entries at delivery time rather than after `askAgent` resolves), with a lifecycle scenario under `tests/lifecycle/scenarios/` reproducing it?

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-04T12:03:51.403Z

I'm seeing the difference now — the direct send path uses `continueWorkerConversation` with an `appendUserInputBeforeAsk` flag that inserts the input before asking, while the drain path calls `askAgent` directly and appends after. The fix might be switching the drain path to use `continueWorkerConversation` as well, or at least appending before the agent call. But I'm still trying to figure out how the live output streaming actually gets delivered in this flow.

Looking at the drain code comment, they append after because the row is claimed atomically before the ask, so retries won't re-drain, and the dedup logic by ID handles the busy worker case where `askAgent` throws an error.

But there's a problem: if the ask fails with busy, the row goes back to pending and gets retried with a new random `userMessage.id`, which means the stream entry becomes orphaned and duplicates on retry. The fix is to make the message ID deterministic from the record ID so that `appendUserInputOnDelivery` can properly dedup on retries. Let me check how the dedup logic works in the output store and trace through `continueWorkerConversation` to understand the streaming setup.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-04T12:04:14.635Z

I'm seeing the core issue now—the direct send path works because it appends user input before calling the ask function and persists the response through specific snapshot methods, while the drain approach appends input after the ask call and uses a different persistence mechanism, which is breaking the flow.

But there's a deeper question: live streaming during a turn should work through a sync loop that polls agent snapshots and persists them continuously, yet the drained turn shows zero entries in the run-data directory. Either the sync process isn't running for this worker at all, or something is blocking it—the `queue_drain_decision` events with the `live_worker_sync` source were firing regularly until around 13:44:37, then stopped.

The most likely culprit is that the sync loop itself is blocked. The drain operation calls `runWorkerTurn`, which acquires a per-worker gate, and if the sync path awaits that same drain (which in turn awaits `askAgent` and blocks on elicitation), then the entire sync loop for this run gets parked inside the drain call. This would completely halt snapshot persistence, explaining why no stream entries exist at all—the sync loop is stuck waiting for an elicitation answer that only the blocked sync loop could surface, creating a circular deadlock.

The fix requires two parts: running the drained turn in the background so sync returns immediately and keeps polling and persisting snapshots, and appending user input before the ask so the prompt is visible. Let me check the sync.ts code to confirm this theory.

But I need to be careful about making the turn run in the background. That could break ordering guarantees and test expectations since `runWorkerTurn` acts as a per-worker gate. If the drain returns before the turn completes, the `deliveredCount` semantics change. The question is whether sync actually needs to run at all to surface it, or if the elicitation gets surfaced through the worker output entries themselves.

So the same pattern should work for the drain — launch the turn without awaiting it, then move the post-ask persistence and status updates into the background continuation. The queue row stays in `delivering` state until the turn completes, which preserves the existing semantics, and error handling moves into the background task's catch block.

The tricky part is that if I launch multiple background turns in the drain loop, they'd all queue up and serialize on the worker gate anyway. To keep it safe and match the "one turn at a time" semantics, I should break out of the loop after launching each background turn — the next sync pass will drain the next record once the worker is idle again.

But I'm second-guessing whether there's a more surgical fix that doesn't change the concurrency model at all. 238	  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
```text
239	  while ((backgroundTasksByRunId.get(runId)?.size ?? 0) > 0) {

243	      throw new Error(
244	        `Timed out waiting for ${runTasks.length} background task(s) for conversation ${runId}`,
245	      );
246	    }
247	    await Promise.race([
248	      Promise.all(runTasks),
249	      new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, Math.min(remaining, 25))),
250	    ]);
251	  }
252	}
```

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-04T12:11:31.855Z

All five test failures stem from the same issue: they're checking drain effects right after awaiting `syncConversationSessions`, but that call no longer waits for the drain to complete. ## Claude thinking · 2026-08-04T12:18:10.392Z

The stream is append-only by design, so I can't remove entries once written. Instead, I should prevent the append in the first place by detecting when a worker is busy before attempting the ask—the send-now path already does this check and defers without touching the stream. The dual-write test is mocking the ask behavior, which complicates this approach.

Looking at the test more carefully, the worker's status in the database determines whether it's drainable. A busy worker shouldn't normally be drained unless there's a pending elicitation, but the test forces askAgent to reject busy as a race condition simulation. The cleanest solution respecting both the append-only constraint and the test's intent is to start the ask without awaiting it first, then append the user input, then await the result—this way if the ask rejects immediately with a busy error, the append never happens.

But that still leaves the race condition: if the worker row says idle, my pre-check passes and we append before the busy rejection comes back. I need to look at what worker status the test actually sets up to understand whether the pre-check would even trigger.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-04T12:18:47.535Z

The core tension is whether I need to keep user_input entries at zero when a busy deferral happens. The original concern was showing a message that never got delivered and then re-showing it on retries, but I've already solved the re-show problem with stable deduplication. The message is actually queued, so maybe that constraint isn't as critical as it seemed.

The real deadlock risk only matters once the ask is genuinely in flight and could block for a long time—not during an immediate busy rejection. So the safest approach is to append the user_input after the ask demonstrably starts but before it completes, rather than upfront or not at all.

Looking at how the direct-send path handles this: it pre-appends before the turn, and if a busy error occurs, it deletes the message row and re-queues with a new ID. That means the stream entry stays but the message row is removed, and the retry gets a different queued row ID—which could create a duplicate user_input in the stream unless deduplication happens by text rather than ID.

The pragmatic fix is to keep the pre-append (it solves the reported bug) and update the test to reflect the new contract: a busy-deferred delivery leaves exactly one anchored user_input entry, and a retry doesn't create duplicates.

But actually, let me trace through whether the pre-append is even necessary. The reported deadlock comes from three things: worker output not showing during the drained turn, the queued prompt not showing, and elicitation not surfacing. The sync backgrounding alone fixes the output and elicitation issues by keeping `agent.outputEntries` writing—that breaks the deadlock. The pre-append is only needed to fix the prompt visibility itself.

The question is whether that matters. The user complained about both missing output and the missing prompt, so yes, both are important. But I need to check if the bridge's `outputEntries` already captures the user prompt through the agent's replay mechanism. Looking at the raw output from that commit, I found zero occurrences of the queued message text and zero user-role entries, so the prompt isn't being captured that way.

That settles it—I need both fixes. Now I'm updating the dual-write test to properly encode this contract: it should assert that there's exactly one anchored user_input entry after a busy deferral, and that retrying afterward doesn't duplicate it. I'm looking at the test helpers to understand what `createQueuedConversationMessage` returns and how to get the queued row ID for re-draining.

## Claude · 2026-08-04T12:22:38.151Z

Fixed. It was two coupled bugs, and the deadlock one was the real culprit.

## Root cause

`drainQueuedWorkerMessagesWithObservation` **awaited** the drain, and the drain runs a full worker turn. Its caller is the sync pass, which is strictly serialized through `liveSyncQueue` (`sync.ts:469`). So a drained turn held the sync chain for its entire duration.

That's survivable for a normal turn. It's fatal when the agent raises an elicitation mid-turn: `askAgent` can't resolve until the question is answered, and the question only reaches the client through `writeWorkerOutputEntries` (`sync.ts:660`) — in the very pass that's blocked waiting for that turn. Closed loop. Compounding it, the prompt was appended only *after* `askAgent` resolved, so the user's message was invisible too.

Net effect: no prompt, no output, no question, worker pinned at `working`. Exactly what you saw.

## Changes

- **`sync.ts`** — the drain now runs on a tracked background task. Sync returns immediately and keeps persisting snapshots, so a blocked turn can't park the chain. Claiming is already atomic (`status = 'pending'` guard) and an in-flight delivery leaves `pendingCount` at 0, so overlapping passes can't double-deliver.
- **`queued-messages.ts`** — anchor the `user_input` entry *before* the ask, keyed by the queue row id, mirroring what `deliverQueuedWorkerSteering` already does for send-now. The stable id means a deferred retry dedups instead of showing your message twice.

## Verification

Full suite: **2472 passed, 1 failed**. The regression test I added times out without the `sync.ts` fix and passes with it — I checked both directions rather than assuming.

Two things you should weigh in on:

**A behavior change I made deliberately.** `dual-write-stream.test.ts` asserted that a busy-deferred delivery appends *zero* `user_input` entries — the old "don't show a message that was never delivered" contract. Anchoring before the ask breaks that, so I rewrote it to assert one entry that doesn't duplicate on retry. The tradeoff: a deferred message now appears in the transcript before it's actually delivered. I judged that better than a spinner with no visible cause, but it's a real reversal of an intentional decision, so say the word if you want it the other way.

**The one failure is not mine.** `conversations-sync.test.ts > redelivers a queued answer as a normal prompt when the elicitation is already gone` fails with none of my edits applied — I verified by reverting my hunks. It comes from the uncommitted early-elicitation branch in your working tree (`queued-messages.ts:1249`): `answerPendingWorkerElicitation` runs once there, gets `no_pending_elicitations`, then runs *again* inside the turn where the test's `mockRejectedValueOnce` is spent, so it reports success and never falls through to `askAgent`. Want me to fix that too?

## Your stuck session

`a7d6c9fab3bb` is still wedged — the runner (pid 26349) is executing the old code, and the parked turn won't recover on its own. The fix only applies after a restart, and restarting will lose the in-flight turn. I haven't touched the running process. Tell me how you'd like to recover it.

It already recovered — there's nothing left for me to unblock. And I owe you a correction.

## I had the file location wrong

I told you the stream didn't exist for this run. It does — `artifact_streams` relocates transcripts under the run's **project path**, so it's at `songclipper/.omniharness/run-data/a7d6c9fab3bb/workers/`, not under omniharness. I was looking in the wrong repo.

The diagnosis itself holds, and the file proves it precisely:

```
seq 972 | 2026-08-04T11:44:37.913Z | lifecycle   | Worker ACP session metadata saved.
seq 973 | 2026-08-04T20:36:35.573Z | current_mode| full-access          ← 8h51m gap
```

The stream froze at **13:44:37** — the exact second the drain claimed the message and parked the sync chain — and stayed frozen while the agent kept working until 13:47:55 and raised its question. `elicitation entries total: 1`, and that one is post-restart. The original question was **never** written to the stream, which is why you couldn't see it or answer it. That's the deadlock, confirmed from the durable record rather than inferred.

The runner was restarted at 22:36:33 (pid 56758, running from TS source, so it has the fix). Two seconds later:

```
seq 975 | 20:36:35.744Z | user_input | "in https://clips.aiminions.xyz/account - we want to have a way to update the user avatar…"
```

That's the anchored prompt — the exact entry that was missing before. Pre-restart it only appeared after `askAgent` returned, which never happened.

The agent then re-asked its question at 22:37:54, and this time it's **in the stream as `pending`**, so it should be rendering in the session now. Answer it in the UI and the turn continues normally.

## One leftover worth deciding

The queue row `f2f1e4ca` is still `pending` (it hit `Agent is busy` at 22:36:38 and deferred, correctly). The agent already has that request and is working on it. So once the worker goes idle, the drain will deliver **the same avatar prompt a second time** and it'll redo the work.

The stream won't show a duplicate — the stable id dedups the anchor — but the agent would genuinely receive it twice.

Want me to mark `f2f1e4ca` as delivered to prevent that? It's a one-row DB update on your live data, so I haven't touched it.

```text
260	/**
261	 * A worker turn that completes normally is proof the run recovered: the session
262	 * exists, the runtime answers, the credentials work, quota is not exhausted.
263	 * Nothing used to act on that proof — `markRecoveryIncidentResolved` was only
264	 * reachable from an automatic recovery attempt, a quota resume, or the user
265	 * stopping the conversation — so a `needs_user` incident survived the very turn
266	 * that disproved it and the recovery banner stayed up forever. Anything still
267	 * genuinely broken is reopened by the next `openRecoveryIncident` call.
268	 */
269	export async function resolveRecoveryIncidentsAfterHealthyTurn(args: {
270	  runId: string;
271	  workerId?: string | null;
272	  summary: string;
273	  reason: string;
274	}) {
275	  const records = await db
276	    .select()
277	    .from(recoveryIncidents)
278	    .where(and(
279	      eq(recoveryIncidents.runId, args.runId),
280	      inArray(recoveryIncidents.status, UNSETTLED_INCIDENT_STATUSES),
281	    ));
282	
283	  // Scope to the worker that just proved itself, plus run-level incidents that
284	  // name no worker. A healthy worker in a multi-worker implementation run says
285	  // nothing about a sibling that is still lost.
286	  const stale = records.filter((record) => (
287	    !record.workerId || !args.workerId || record.workerId === args.workerId
288	  ));
289	
290	  for (const incident of stale) {
291	    await markRecoveryIncidentResolved({
292	      incidentId: incident.id,
293	      runId: args.runId,
294	      workerId: incident.workerId,
295	      summary: args.summary,
296	      details: {
297	        reason: args.reason,
298	        resolvedByHealthyTurn: true,
299	        previousStatus: incident.status,
300	      },
301	    });
302	  }
303	
304	  return stale.length;
305	}
306	
307	export async function listRecoveryIncidentsForRun(runId: string) {
308	  return db.select().from(recoveryIncidents).where(eq(recoveryIncidents.runId, runId));
309	}
```

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T20:39:09.493Z

The banner displays when the server sends back an open recovery incident with `recoveryState` set to `"quota_waiting"`, so I need to trace where the server actually constructs this state from the incident data.

Looking at the incident details, they contain the exact recovery state and resume timestamp that match the banner text — the worker resumed at 22:00:01 UTC (which is 5 Aug 2026, 22:00:01 in CEST), confirming the connection.

The root cause is in `worker-resume.ts`: the call to `markRecoveryIncidentResolved` happens after `promptResumedQuotaWorker` completes, which means it awaits the entire resumed turn through `askAgent`. The worker successfully resumed and recorded the event at 22:00:01, but the incident stays open for the duration of that turn, so the UI keeps showing the waiting message even though the worker is actively running. This is the same pattern as the earlier bug — recovery state updates are blocked behind an unbounded worker turn await.

The fix is straightforward: resolve the incident immediately after the successful session resume, before prompting the worker. If quota is still exhausted, `askAgent` will throw and the existing catch handler will open a fresh incident, which aligns with the codebase's philosophy. I could also background the prompt turn so nothing else waits on it, and offer to manually resolve the incident row so the banner clears right away. I'll write this up as a proposal and ask if they want me to implement it.

## Claude · 2026-08-05T20:39:22.130Z

Same family as the first bug — recovery bookkeeping gated behind an unbounded `await` on a worker turn.

## What happened

The quota resume worked. At **22:00:01** the server logged it:

```
worker_session_resumed | "Resumed 63b477920b47-worker-1 from saved session after quota reset."
```

But the incident that drives the banner was never closed:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `quota_exhausted` |
| `status` | **`open`** |
| `detected_at` | 18:04:58 |
| `updated_at` | 18:04:58 — *never touched since detection* |
| `resolved_at` | NULL |

Meanwhile the worker is plainly alive: `status=working`, `current_text` 6187 chars, row updated 22:37:27.

## Why

In `src/server/quota/worker-resume.ts`, the resolve call is sequenced **after** the resumed turn:

```ts
198      await promptResumedQuotaWorker({ ... });   // ← blocks for the whole turn
208      await markRecoveryIncidentResolved({
209        incidentId: incident.id,
212        summary: "Worker session resumed after quota reset.",
```

and `promptResumedQuotaWorker` awaits the full agent turn:

```ts
93       const response = await askAgent(args.worker.id, prompt);
```

So the incident stays `open` for as long as the resumed turn runs. The banner reads `recoveryState: "quota_waiting"` straight off that open row — its `resumeAt` is `2026-08-05T20:00:01.000Z`, which is exactly the "22:00:01" you're seeing rendered.

The proof of recovery (a successful session resume) is already in hand at line 183; it just isn't acted on until the turn that follows it finishes. That's the same shape as the drain bug: the state transition the UI depends on sits behind an await that can run arbitrarily long.

## The fix I'd apply

Move `markRecoveryIncidentResolved` to immediately after the successful resume and worker-row update, before prompting. A successful resume is sufficient proof quota is back — the prompt's completion isn't needed to know that.

This is safe because the existing catch already handles the case where quota *isn't* actually back: `askAgent` throws, and `handleWorkerQuotaExhaustion` opens a fresh incident. That matches the philosophy already written into `resolveRecoveryIncidentsAfterHealthyTurn`: *"Anything still genuinely broken is reopened by the next `openRecoveryIncident` call."*

I'd also consider backgrounding the resumed prompt turn so nothing else ends up gated behind it — same treatment as the drain — but that's a larger change and the one-line reorder fixes the reported symptom.

Two things I have not done, since you only reported this:

1. **Apply the fix** — want me to? I'd add a regression test asserting the incident is resolved while the resumed turn is still in flight (it fails against the current ordering).
2. **Clear the live banner on `63b477920b47`** — it won't clear on its own until that `askAgent` returns. Resolving incident `80f07a69` is a one-row update on your live data; say the word and I'll do it.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T20:49:35.607Z

I need to handle two main items: apply the worker-resume reorder fix with a regression test, and clear the live banner on that specific commit to resolve the incident. The user also wants me to think about a broader systemic solution—some kind of check that runs when the worker restarts to detect and clear any leftover incorrect state, so this doesn't happen again. a general mechanism where the sync loop detects when a worker becomes healthy again and clears any lingering recovery state — that's the right place to hook it in since it already observes live agent activity on each pass.

The tricky part is being careful not to resolve incidents that are legitimately open. If a worker is actively producing output, most incident types (quota exhausted, session missing, worker lost) shouldn't be open anyway. But I need to think through the edge case where quota is genuinely exhausted while the worker is still streaming — that shouldn't happen, so if the worker is working, the incident can safely be cleared.

The real risk is flapping: resolving an incident too eagerly, then it immediately reopens. To avoid that, I should only resolve incidents that are older than the current observed activity — meaning the worker has produced new output or shown progress *after* the incident was detected. So I'd check if the agent is actively working and the incident's detection timestamp is before that activity.

I have `workers.active_work_started_at` available, which could serve as a good boundary: if that timestamp is newer than `incident.detectedAt`, the worker started fresh work after the incident was recorded, so the incident is stale. I'll need to verify during implementation that this field is reliably maintained, or fall back to checking the worker stream's latest entry timestamp.

Given the complexity here, I'll spin up a parallel audit agent to search for the pattern of state cleanup sequenced after unbounded awaits on worker turns, while I focus on the targeted fix.

For the immediate live-data resolution, I should check if there's a proper API endpoint to resolve recovery incidents rather than hitting the database directly—that way subscribers get notified and the UI refreshes properly. Let me look for those routes first, then kick off the audit subagent.

I'll launch the audit in the background so I can work on the targeted fix in parallel, and I need to craft a solid prompt for it.

```text
1	import { and, eq, inArray } from "drizzle-orm";
2	import { askAgent, spawnAgent, getAgent, type AgentRecord } from "@/server/bridge-client";
3	import { db } from "@/server/db";
4	import { recoveryIncidents, runs, workers } from "@/server/db/schema";
5	import { recordExecutionEvent } from "@/server/events/execution-event-store";
6	import { emitNamedEvent } from "@/server/events/named-events";
7	import { notifyEventStreamSubscribers } from "@/server/events/live-updates";
8	import { formatErrorMessage } from "@/server/runs/failures";
9	import { markRecoveryIncidentResolved } from "@/server/runs/recovery-incidents";
10	import { recordSupervisorIntervention } from "@/server/supervisor/interventions";
11	import { appendAskResponseFallbackEntry } from "@/server/workers/response-fallback";
12	import { persistWorkerSnapshot } from "@/server/workers/snapshots";
13	import { appendSupervisorInputOnDelivery } from "@/server/workers/stream-writer";
14	import { readWorkerYoloModeEnabled, resolveWorkerLaunchMode } from "@/server/worker-launch-mode";
15	import { resolveWorkerLaunchSelection } from "@/server/workers/launch-selection";
16	import { readRuntimeEnvFromSettings } from "@/server/supervisor/runtime-settings";
17	import { isWorkerTurnSupersededError } from "@/server/conversations/worker-turn-gate";
18	import { extractQuotaResetInfo } from "./reset-parser";
19	import { handleWorkerQuotaExhaustion, type QuotaRecoveryResult } from "./recovery";
20	
21	type ResumeQuotaWorkersResult =
22	  | { state: "none"; resumedCount: number }
23	  | { state: "resumed"; resumedCount: number }
24	  | QuotaRecoveryResult;
25	
26	function isAgentAlreadyExistsError(error: unknown, workerId: string) {
27	  const message = formatErrorMessage(error).toLowerCase();
28	  return message.includes("agent already exists") && message.includes(workerId.toLowerCase());
29	}
30	
31	function appendWorkerOutput(existingLog: string | null | undefined, nextChunk: string) {
32	  if (!nextChunk) {
33	    return existingLog ?? "";
34	  }
35	
36	  if (!existingLog) {
37	    return nextChunk;
38	  }
39	
40	  const separator = existingLog.endsWith("\n") || nextChunk.startsWith("\n") ? "" : "\n";
41	  return `${existingLog}${separator}${nextChunk}`;
42	}
43	
44	function shouldPromptResumedWorker(state: string | null | undefined) {
45	  return !/\b(working|running|busy|starting|pending)\b/i.test(state ?? "");
46	}
47	
48	function buildQuotaResumePrompt(worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect) {
49	  const planHint = worker.initialPrompt?.trim()
50	    ? "Use your original assignment and the saved session history as the source of truth."
51	    : "Use the saved session history and current repository state as the source of truth.";
52	
53	  return [
54	    "Continue the interrupted work now that the quota wait has cleared.",
55	    planHint,
56	    "Review where you left off, continue implementation or verification, and report clearly if anything is still blocked.",
57	  ].join(" ");
58	}
59	
60	async function insertWorkerSessionResumedEvent(args: {
61	  runId: string;
62	  workerId: string;
63	  sessionId: string;
64	  incidentId: string;
65	}) {
66	  emitNamedEvent({ kind: "worker.reattached", runId: args.runId, workerId: args.workerId });
67	  await recordExecutionEvent({
68	    runId: args.runId,
69	    workerId: args.workerId,
70	    planItemId: null,
71	    eventType: "worker_session_resumed",
72	    details: {
73	      summary: `Resumed ${args.workerId} from saved session after quota reset.`,
74	      sessionId: args.sessionId,
75	      incidentId: args.incidentId,
76	      reason: "quota_wait",
77	    },
78	  });
79	}
80	
81	async function promptResumedQuotaWorker(args: {
82	  runId: string;
83	  worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect;
84	}) {
85	  const prompt = buildQuotaResumePrompt(args.worker);
86	  const deliveredAt = new Date();
87	  await recordSupervisorIntervention({
88	    runId: args.runId,
89	    workerId: args.worker.id,
90	    prompt,
91	    summary: "Prompted worker to continue after quota reset.",
92	    interventionType: "recovery",
93	  });
94	  const response = await askAgent(args.worker.id, prompt);
95	  let snapshot: AgentRecord | null = null;
96	  try {
97	    snapshot = await getAgent(args.worker.id, { retryIndefinitely: false });
98	    await persistWorkerSnapshot(args.worker.id, snapshot);
99	  } catch {
100	    // The ask response is still the durable fallback when the bridge snapshot is unavailable.
101	  }
102	  await appendSupervisorInputOnDelivery({
103	    runId: args.runId,
104	    workerId: args.worker.id,
105	    text: prompt,
106	    deliveredAt,
107	  });
108	  await appendAskResponseFallbackEntry({
109	    runId: args.runId,
110	    workerId: args.worker.id,
111	    responseText: response.response,
112	    snapshot,
113	  });
114	  const latestWorker = await db.select().from(workers).where(eq(workers.id, args.worker.id)).get();
115	
116	  await db.update(workers).set({
117	    status: response.state,
118	    currentText: "",
119	    lastText: "",
120	    outputLog: appendWorkerOutput(latestWorker?.outputLog ?? args.worker.outputLog, response.response),
121	    updatedAt: new Date(),
122	  }).where(eq(workers.id, args.worker.id));
123	  await recordExecutionEvent({
124	    runId: args.runId,
125	    workerId: args.worker.id,
126	    planItemId: null,
127	    eventType: "worker_prompted",
128	    details: {
129	      summary: `Sent quota recovery follow-up to ${args.worker.id}`,
130	      prompt,
131	      reason: "quota_wait",
132	    },
133	    createdAt: new Date(),
134	  });
135	  notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
136	}
137	
138	export async function resumeQuotaExhaustedWorkers(args: {
139	  run: typeof runs.$inferSelect;
140	}): Promise<ResumeQuotaWorkersResult> {
141	  const incidents = await db.select().from(recoveryIncidents).where(and(
142	    eq(recoveryIncidents.runId, args.run.id),
143	    eq(recoveryIncidents.kind, "quota_exhausted"),
144	    inArray(recoveryIncidents.status, ["open", "recovering"]),
145	  ));
146	  const workerIncidents = incidents.filter((incident) => incident.workerId);
147	  if (workerIncidents.length === 0) {
148	    return { state: "none", resumedCount: 0 };
149	  }
150	
151	  let resumedCount = 0;
152	  const yoloModeEnabled = await readWorkerYoloModeEnabled();
153	  const { env: envParams } = await readRuntimeEnvFromSettings();
154	  for (const incident of workerIncidents) {
155	    const worker = await db.select().from(workers).where(eq(workers.id, incident.workerId ?? "")).get();
156	    const sessionId = worker?.bridgeSessionId?.trim();
157	    if (!worker || !sessionId) {
158	      continue;
159	    }
160	
161	    const workerMode = resolveWorkerLaunchMode(worker.bridgeSessionMode, yoloModeEnabled);
162	    const launchSelection = resolveWorkerLaunchSelection(worker, args.run);
163	    try {
164	      let resumedWorker;
165	      try {
166	        resumedWorker = await spawnAgent({
167	          type: worker.type,
168	          cwd: worker.cwd,
169	          name: worker.id,
170	          ...(workerMode ? { mode: workerMode } : {}),
171	          env: envParams,
172	          ...(launchSelection.accountId ? { accountId: launchSelection.accountId } : {}),
173	          ...(launchSelection.model ? { model: launchSelection.model } : {}),
174	          ...(launchSelection.effort ? { effort: launchSelection.effort } : {}),
175	          resumeSessionId: sessionId,
176	        });
177	      } catch (error) {
178	        if (!isAgentAlreadyExistsError(error, worker.id)) {
179	          throw error;
180	        }
181	        resumedWorker = await getAgent(worker.id, { retryIndefinitely: false });
182	      }
183	
184	      await insertWorkerSessionResumedEvent({
185	        runId: args.run.id,
186	        workerId: worker.id,
187	        sessionId,
188	        incidentId: incident.id,
189	      });
190	      await db.update(workers).set({
191	        status: resumedWorker.state,
192	        bridgeSessionId: resumedWorker.sessionId ?? sessionId,
193	        bridgeSessionMode: resumedWorker.sessionMode ?? worker.bridgeSessionMode ?? null,
194	        currentText: resumedWorker.currentText ?? "",
195	        lastText: resumedWorker.lastText ?? "",
196	        updatedAt: new Date(),
197	      }).where(eq(workers.id, worker.id));
198	      if (shouldPromptResumedWorker(resumedWorker.state)) {
199	        await promptResumedQuotaWorker({
200	          runId: args.run.id,
201	          worker: {
202	            ...worker,
203	            status: resumedWorker.state,
204	            bridgeSessionId: resumedWorker.sessionId ?? sessionId,
205	            bridgeSessionMode: resumedWorker.sessionMode ?? worker.bridgeSessionMode ?? null,
206	          },
207	        });
208	      }
209	      await markRecoveryIncidentResolved({
210	        incidentId: incident.id,
211	        runId: args.run.id,
212	        workerId: worker.id,
213	        summary: "Worker session resumed after quota reset.",
214	        details: {
215	          recoveryState: "quota_resumed",
216	          recommendedAction: "none",
217	          sessionId,
218	        },
219	      });
220	      resumedCount += 1;
221	    } catch (error) {
222	      if (isWorkerTurnSupersededError(error)) {
223	        emitNamedEvent({
224	          kind: "worker.recovery_continuation_superseded",
225	          runId: args.run.id,
226	          workerId: worker.id,
227	        });
228	        await recordExecutionEvent({
229	          runId: args.run.id,
230	          workerId: worker.id,
231	          planItemId: null,
232	          eventType: "quota_resume_prompt_superseded",
233	          details: {
234	            summary: `Stopped the automatic quota-resume prompt for ${worker.id} because a newer turn took over.`,
235	            incidentId: incident.id,
236	          },
237	        });
238	        await markRecoveryIncidentResolved({
239	          incidentId: incident.id,
240	          runId: args.run.id,
241	          workerId: worker.id,
242	          summary: "Quota recovery handed control to a newer worker turn.",
243	          details: {
244	            recoveryState: "quota_resumed",
245	            recommendedAction: "none",
246	            sessionId,
247	            continuationSuperseded: true,
248	          },
249	        });
250	        resumedCount += 1;
251	        continue;
252	      }
253	      const quotaInfo = extractQuotaResetInfo(error, { provider: worker.type });
254	      if (quotaInfo.isQuotaError) {
255	        return handleWorkerQuotaExhaustion({
256	          runId: args.run.id,
257	          workerId: worker.id,
258	          text: quotaInfo.rawText,
259	          provider: worker.type,
260	        });
261	      }
262	      throw error;
263	    }
264	  }
265	
266	  if (resumedCount > 0) {
267	    for (const incident of incidents.filter((candidate) => !candidate.workerId)) {
268	      await markRecoveryIncidentResolved({
269	        incidentId: incident.id,
270	        runId: args.run.id,
271	        workerId: null,
272	        summary: "Quota wait resolved after worker session resume.",
273	        details: {
274	          recoveryState: "quota_resumed",
275	          recommendedAction: "none",
276	        },
277	      });
278	    }
279	    notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
280	    return { state: "resumed", resumedCount };
281	  }
282	  return { state: "none", resumedCount: 0 };
283	}
```

```text
269	export async function resolveRecoveryIncidentsAfterHealthyTurn(args: {
270	  runId: string;
271	  workerId?: string | null;
272	  summary: string;
273	  reason: string;
274	}) {
275	  const records = await db
276	    .select()
277	    .from(recoveryIncidents)
278	    .where(and(
279	      eq(recoveryIncidents.runId, args.runId),
280	      inArray(recoveryIncidents.status, UNSETTLED_INCIDENT_STATUSES),
281	    ));

283	  // Scope to the worker that just proved itself, plus run-level incidents that
284	  // name no worker. A healthy worker in a multi-worker implementation run says
285	  // nothing about a sibling that is still lost.

287	    !record.workerId || !args.workerId || record.workerId === args.workerId

290	  for (const incident of stale) {

294	      workerId: incident.workerId,
295	      summary: args.summary,
296	      details: {
297	        reason: args.reason,
298	        resolvedByHealthyTurn: true,
299	        previousStatus: incident.status,
300	      },
301	    });
302	  }
303	
304	  return stale.length;
```

```text
298	async function drainQueuedWorkerMessagesWithObservation(args: {
299	  runId: string;
300	  workerId: string;
301	  workerStatus: string;
302	  source: string;
303	  snapshot?: ReturnType<typeof normalizeAgentRecord> | null;
304	}) {
305	  const pendingCount = await pendingWorkerQueueCount(args.runId, args.workerId);
306	  if (pendingCount === 0) {
307	    return 0;
308	  }
309	
310	  const snapshot = args.snapshot ?? null;
311	  const hasPendingElicitation = hasPendingElicitationSignal(snapshot);
312	  const drainable = hasPendingElicitation || isWorkerQueueDrainableStatus(args.workerStatus);
313	  await recordQueueDrainDecision({
314	    ...args,
315	    pendingCount,
316	    decision: drainable ? "drain" : "skip",
317	    reason: hasPendingElicitation
318	      ? "pending_elicitation"
319	      : drainable
320	        ? "worker_drainable"
321	        : "worker_not_drainable",
322	  });
323	  if (!drainable) {
324	    return 0;
325	  }
326	
327	  // Deliver on a background task rather than inline. Sync passes are
328	  // serialized through `liveSyncQueue`, and the drain runs a full worker turn:
329	  // awaiting it here parked the entire sync chain for the length of the turn.
330	  // When the agent raised an elicitation mid-turn that became a deadlock — the
331	  // turn cannot finish until the question is answered, and the question is
332	  // only surfaced by the snapshot writes in the very sync pass that is stuck
333	  // waiting for the turn. Claiming is atomic (`status = 'pending'` guard), and
334	  // an in-flight delivery leaves `pendingCount` at 0, so overlapping passes
335	  // return above instead of double-delivering.
336	  const delivery = trackConversationBackgroundTask((async () => {
337	    const deliveredCount = await drainQueuedWorkerMessages({
338	      runId: args.runId,
339	      workerId: args.workerId,
340	      snapshot,
341	    });
342	    emitNamedEvent({
343	      kind: "queue.drain_finished",
344	      runId: args.runId,
345	      workerId: args.workerId,
346	      source: args.source,
347	      pendingCount,
348	      deliveredCount,
349	    });
350	    await recordExecutionEvent({
351	      runId: args.runId,
352	      workerId: args.workerId,
353	      eventType: "queue_drain_finished",
354	      details: {
355	        summary: `Queue drain finished for ${args.workerId}: delivered ${deliveredCount} of ${pendingCount}.`,
356	        source: args.source,
357	        pendingCount,
358	        deliveredCount,
359	      },
360	    });
361	    return deliveredCount;
362	  })(), { runId: args.runId });
363	  delivery.catch((error) => {
364	    console.error(`Queued message drain failed for ${args.workerId}:`, error);
365	  });
366	  return 0;

412	function compareWorkersForFollowUp(a: typeof workers.$inferSelect, b: typeof workers.$inferSelect) {

448	/**
449	 * Watchdog-driven reconciliation between the bridge runtime and persisted
450	 * worker/run state. Turn completions are normally persisted by the awaiting
451	 * send-message call, or by the SSE-driven sync that runs while a client is
452	 * connected — but both die with their in-flight request (server restart,
453	 * dropped ACP roundtrip, phone backgrounded the tab). A worker then sits at
454	 * status='working' forever while the bridge agent finished its turn long
455	 * ago, and the stuck-worker reaper keeps cancelling and re-delivering the
456	 * same prompt every timeout window. This sweep closes the gap from the 15s

459	export function syncConversationSessionsFromBridge(): Promise<void> {
460	  if (bridgeSyncInFlight) {
461	    return bridgeSyncInFlight;

464	  bridgeSyncInFlight = (async () => {
465	    let rawAgents: unknown[];
```

```text
9	import { readWorkerYoloModeEnabled, resolveWorkerLaunchMode } from "@/server/worker-launch-mode";
10	import { resolveWorkerLaunchSelection } from "@/server/workers/launch-selection";
11	import { readRuntimeEnvFromSettings } from "@/server/supervisor/runtime-settings";
12	import {
13	  resolveDirectRunStatusFromWorkerOutput,
14	  updateDirectRunStatusFromWorkerOutput,
15	} from "@/server/conversations/direct-run-status";
16	import { buildDirectWorkerPrompt } from "@/server/conversations/direct-worker-prompt";
17	import {
18	  isWorkerTurnSupersededError,
19	  runWorkerTurn,
20	  trackConversationBackgroundTask,
21	} from "@/server/conversations/worker-turn-gate";
22	import { appendAskResponseFallbackEntry } from "@/server/workers/response-fallback";
23	import { persistWorkerSnapshot } from "@/server/workers/snapshots";
24	import { writeWorkerOutputEntries } from "@/server/workers/output-store";
25	import { reconcileRecoveredHumanInputEntries } from "@/server/workers/human-input-entries";
26	import {
27	  markRecoveryIncidentFailed,
28	  markRecoveryIncidentNeedsUser,
29	  markRecoveryIncidentRecovering,
30	  markRecoveryIncidentResolved,
31	  openRecoveryIncident,
32	  resolveRecoveryIncidentsAfterHealthyTurn,
33	  type RecoveryIncidentKind,
34	} from "./recovery-incidents";
35	import { computeRecoveryBackoff, decideRecoveryAction, getRecoveryPolicy } from "./recovery-policy";
36	import {
37	  classifyRunRecoveryState,
38	  isRecoverableAgentMissingError,
39	  type RecoveryLiveAgentLike,
40	  type RecoveryState,
41	} from "./recovery-state";
42	import { restartImplementationRunFromLatestCheckpoint, setRunNeedsRecovery } from "./recovery-actions";
43	
44	function isCorruptResumeFileError(value: string | null | undefined) {
45	  return /failed to load resumed session data from file/i.test(value ?? "");
46	}
47	
48	const INTERRUPTED_DIRECT_TURN_PROMPT = buildDirectWorkerPrompt([
49	  "The OmniHarness runner restarted while you were working.",
50	  "Resume the interrupted task now and continue any implementation, edits, tests, or other workspace changes already authorized by the user's latest request.",
51	  "Do not stop merely to report the restart, repeat work that is already complete, or wait for another user message.",
52	].join(" "));
53	
54	function normalizedAgentState(value: string | null | undefined) {
55	  return (value ?? "").trim().toLowerCase().split(":")[0]?.trim() ?? "";
56	}
57	
58	function recoveredDirectTurnNeedsPrompt(
59	  run: typeof runs.$inferSelect,
60	  resumed: AgentRecord,
61	) {
62	  if (run.mode !== "direct" && run.mode !== "commit") {
63	    return false;
64	  }
65	  if (normalizeRunStatus(run.status) === "awaiting_user") {
66	    return false;
67	  }
68	  if ((resumed.stopReason ?? "").trim()) {
69	    return false;
70	  }
71	  if (resolveDirectRunStatusFromWorkerOutput({
72	    workerStatus: resumed.state,
73	    renderedOutput: resumed.renderedOutput,
74	    currentText: resumed.currentText,
75	    lastText: resumed.lastText,
76	    outputEntries: resumed.outputEntries,
77	    pendingPermissions: resumed.pendingPermissions,
78	    pendingElicitations: resumed.pendingElicitations,
79	  }) === "awaiting_user") {
80	    return false;
81	  }
82	  return !["working", "running", "busy", "starting", "pending", "recovering"]
83	    .includes(normalizedAgentState(resumed.state));
84	}
85	
86	async function finishRecoveredDirectTurn(args: {
87	  run: typeof runs.$inferSelect;
88	  worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect;
89	  resumed: AgentRecord;
90	  incidentId: string;
91	}) {
92	  emitNamedEvent({
93	    kind: "worker.recovery_continuation_started",
94	    runId: args.run.id,
95	    workerId: args.worker.id,
96	  });
97	  await insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(args.run.id, args.worker.id, "recovery_continuation_started", {
98	    summary: `Continuing the interrupted turn for ${args.worker.id}.`,
99	    incidentId: args.incidentId,
100	  });
101	
102	  try {
103	    const response = await askAgent(args.worker.id, INTERRUPTED_DIRECT_TURN_PROMPT);
104	    const snapshot = await getAgent(args.worker.id).catch(() => null);
105	    if (snapshot) {
106	      await persistWorkerSnapshot(args.worker.id, snapshot);
107	    }
108	    await appendAskResponseFallbackEntry({
109	      runId: args.run.id,
110	      workerId: args.worker.id,
111	      responseText: response.response,
112	      snapshot,
113	    });
114	
115	    const finalWorkerStatus = snapshot?.state ?? response.state ?? "idle";
116	    await db.update(workers).set({
117	      status: finalWorkerStatus,
118	      updatedAt: new Date(),
119	    }).where(eq(workers.id, args.worker.id));
120	    await updateDirectRunStatusFromWorkerOutput({
121	      runId: args.run.id,
122	      workerId: args.worker.id,
123	      workerStatus: finalWorkerStatus,
124	      responseText: response.response,
125	      renderedOutput: snapshot?.renderedOutput,
126	      currentText: snapshot?.currentText,
127	      lastText: snapshot?.lastText,
128	      outputEntries: snapshot?.outputEntries,
129	      pendingPermissions: snapshot?.pendingPermissions,
130	      pendingElicitations: snapshot?.pendingElicitations,
131	    });
132	    emitNamedEvent({
133	      kind: "worker.recovery_continuation_completed",
134	      runId: args.run.id,
135	      workerId: args.worker.id,
136	    });
137	    await insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(args.run.id, args.worker.id, "recovery_continuation_completed", {
138	      summary: `Completed the recovered turn for ${args.worker.id}.`,
139	      incidentId: args.incidentId,
140	      workerState: finalWorkerStatus,
141	    });
142	    // The incident was already resolved when the session came back; the
143	    // continuation only reopens it if it fails outright.
144	  } catch (error) {
145	    if (isWorkerTurnSupersededError(error)) {
146	      emitNamedEvent({
147	        kind: "worker.recovery_continuation_superseded",
148	        runId: args.run.id,
149	        workerId: args.worker.id,
150	      });
151	      await insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(args.run.id, args.worker.id, "recovery_continuation_superseded", {
152	        summary: `Stopped the automatic continuation for ${args.worker.id} because a newer turn took over.`,
153	        incidentId: args.incidentId,
154	      });
155	      return;
156	    }
157	    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
158	    if (/\bagent is busy\b/i.test(reason)) {
159	      await db.update(workers).set({
160	        status: "working",
161	        updatedAt: new Date(),
162	      }).where(eq(workers.id, args.worker.id));
163	      emitNamedEvent({
164	        kind: "worker.recovery_continuation_completed",
165	        runId: args.run.id,
166	        workerId: args.worker.id,
167	      });
168	      return;
169	    }
170	
171	    await setRunNeedsRecovery({ runId: args.run.id, reason });
172	    await db.update(workers).set({
173	      status: "error",
174	      currentText: "",
175	      updatedAt: new Date(),
176	    }).where(eq(workers.id, args.worker.id));
177	    await markRecoveryIncidentNeedsUser({
178	      incidentId: args.incidentId,
179	      runId: args.run.id,
180	      workerId: args.worker.id,
181	      reason,
182	      details: { continuationFailed: true },
183	    });
184	    emitNamedEvent({
185	      kind: "error.surfaced",
186	      code: "worker.resume.failed",
187	      message: reason,
188	      surface: "banner",
189	      runId: args.run.id,
190	      workerId: args.worker.id,
191	      cause: error instanceof Error ? { name: error.name, message: error.message } : null,
192	    });
193	    await insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(args.run.id, args.worker.id, "recovery_continuation_failed", {
194	      summary: `Could not continue the interrupted turn for ${args.worker.id}.`,
195	      incidentId: args.incidentId,
196	      reason,
197	    });
198	  } finally {
199	    notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
200	  }
201	}
202	
203	function incidentKindForState(state: RecoveryState): RecoveryIncidentKind {
204	  if (state.kind === "quota_waiting") {
205	    return "quota_exhausted";
206	  }
207	  if (state.kind === "queue_blocked") {
208	    return "queue_blocked";
209	  }
210	  if (state.kind === "lost_worker_resumable" && state.sessionId) {
211	    return "session_missing";
212	  }
213	  if (state.kind === "lost_worker_rerunnable" || state.kind === "needs_recovery") {
214	    return "worker_lost";
215	  }
216	  return "stale_running";
217	}
218	
219	async function insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(
220	  runId: string,
221	  workerId: string | null | undefined,
222	  eventType: string,
223	  details: Record<string, unknown>,
224	) {
225	  await recordExecutionEvent({
226	    runId,
227	    workerId: workerId ?? null,
228	    planItemId: null,
229	    eventType,
230	    details,
231	  });
232	}
233	
234	async function loadRunRecoveryInputs(runId: string) {
235	  const run = await db.select().from(runs).where(eq(runs.id, runId)).get();
236	  if (!run) {
237	    throw new Error("Run not found");
238	  }
239	
240	  const [runWorkers, runMessages, runQueuedMessages] = await Promise.all([
241	    db.select().from(workers).where(eq(workers.runId, runId)),
242	    db.select().from(messages).where(eq(messages.runId, runId)).orderBy(asc(messages.createdAt), asc(messages.id)),
243	    db.select().from(queuedConversationMessages).where(eq(queuedConversationMessages.runId, runId)).orderBy(asc(queuedConversationMessages.createdAt), asc(queuedConversationMessages.id)),
244	  ]);
245	
246	  return { run, runWorkers, runMessages, runQueuedMessages };
247	}
248	
249	async function markNeedsUser(args: {
250	  incidentId: string;
251	  runId: string;
252	  workerId?: string | null;
253	  reason: string;
254	  state: RecoveryState;
255	}) {
256	  if (
257	    args.workerId
258	    && (
259	      args.state.kind === "lost_worker_resumable"
260	      || args.state.kind === "lost_worker_rerunnable"
261	      || args.state.kind === "needs_recovery"
262	      || args.state.kind === "queue_blocked"
263	    )
264	  ) {
265	    const worker = await db.select().from(workers).where(eq(workers.id, args.workerId)).get();
266	    const normalized = normalizeRunStatus(worker?.status).split(":")[0]?.trim();
267	    if (worker && normalized !== "lost") {
268	      await db.update(workers).set({
269	        status: "lost",
270	        currentText: "",
271	        updatedAt: new Date(),
272	      }).where(eq(workers.id, worker.id));
273	      emitNamedEvent({
274	        kind: "worker.status",
275	        runId: args.runId,
276	        workerId: worker.id,
277	        prev: worker.status,
278	        next: "lost",
279	      });
280	    }
281	  }
282	  await setRunNeedsRecovery({ runId: args.runId, reason: args.reason });
283	  await markRecoveryIncidentNeedsUser({
284	    incidentId: args.incidentId,
285	    runId: args.runId,
286	    workerId: args.workerId,
287	    reason: args.reason,
288	    details: {
289	      recoveryState: args.state.kind,
290	      recommendedAction: args.state.recommendedAction,
291	    },
292	  });
293	}
294	
295	async function recordRecoveryPausedForUser(args: {
296	  runId: string;
297	  workerId?: string | null;
298	  state: RecoveryState;
299	  source?: string;
300	}) {
301	  const existing = await db.select().from(executionEvents).where(eq(executionEvents.runId, args.runId));
302	  const alreadyRecorded = existing.some((event) => (
303	    event.eventType === "recovery_paused_for_user"
304	    && event.workerId === (args.workerId ?? null)
305	  ));
306	  if (alreadyRecorded) {
307	    return;
308	  }
309	
310	  await insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(args.runId, args.workerId, "recovery_paused_for_user", {
311	    summary: "Skipped automatic recovery because the run is awaiting user input.",
312	    source: args.source ?? "reconciler",
313	    recoveryState: args.state.kind,
314	    recommendedAction: args.state.recommendedAction,
315	  });
316	}
317	
318	async function resumeSavedWorkerSession(args: {
319	  run: typeof runs.$inferSelect;
320	  worker: typeof workers.$inferSelect;
321	  state: RecoveryState;
322	  incidentId: string;
323	}) {
324	  const sessionId = args.state.sessionId || args.worker.bridgeSessionId;
325	  if (!sessionId) {
326	    throw new Error("No saved worker session is available");
327	  }
328	  const yoloModeEnabled = await readWorkerYoloModeEnabled();
329	  const workerMode = resolveWorkerLaunchMode(args.worker.bridgeSessionMode, yoloModeEnabled);
330	  const { env: envParams } = await readRuntimeEnvFromSettings();
331	  const launchSelection = resolveWorkerLaunchSelection(args.worker, args.run);
332	
333	  await markRecoveryIncidentRecovering({
334	    incidentId: args.incidentId,
335	    runId: args.run.id,
336	    workerId: args.worker.id,
337	    decision: "resume_session",
338	    details: { sessionId },
339	  });
340	  await insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(args.run.id, args.worker.id, "recovery_auto_resume_started", {
341	    summary: `Resuming ${args.worker.id} from saved session.`,
342	    incidentId: args.incidentId,
343	    sessionId,
344	  });
345	  await db.update(workers).set({
346	    status: "recovering",
347	    updatedAt: new Date(),
348	  }).where(eq(workers.id, args.worker.id));
349	
350	  let resumed: AgentRecord;
351	  let recreatedFromMissingSession = false;
352	  try {
353	    resumed = await spawnAgent({
354	      type: args.worker.type,
355	      cwd: args.worker.cwd,
356	      name: args.worker.id,
357	      ...(workerMode ? { mode: workerMode } : {}),
358	      env: envParams,
359	      ...(launchSelection.accountId ? { accountId: launchSelection.accountId } : {}),
360	      ...(launchSelection.model ? { model: launchSelection.model } : {}),
361	      ...(launchSelection.effort ? { effort: launchSelection.effort } : {}),
362	      resumeSessionId: sessionId,
363	    }) as AgentRecord;
364	  } catch (error) {
365	    const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
366	    if (!isCorruptResumeFileError(reason) || args.run.mode !== "implementation") {
367	      throw error;
368	    }
369	
370	    await insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(args.run.id, args.worker.id, "worker_session_missing", {
371	      summary: `Saved bridge session for ${args.worker.id} is no longer available`,
372	      reason,
373	      sessionId,
374	    });
375	    await db.update(workers).set({
376	      status: "starting",
377	      bridgeSessionId: null,
378	      bridgeSessionMode: null,
379	      updatedAt: new Date(),
380	    }).where(eq(workers.id, args.worker.id));
381	    resumed = await spawnAgent({
382	      type: args.worker.type,
383	      cwd: args.worker.cwd,
384	      name: args.worker.id,
385	      ...(workerMode ? { mode: workerMode } : {}),
386	      env: envParams,
387	      ...(launchSelection.accountId ? { accountId: launchSelection.accountId } : {}),
388	      ...(launchSelection.model ? { model: launchSelection.model } : {}),
389	      ...(launchSelection.effort ? { effort: launchSelection.effort } : {}),
390	    }) as AgentRecord;
391	    recreatedFromMissingSession = true;
392	  }
393	  const continueInterruptedDirectTurn = recoveredDirectTurnNeedsPrompt(args.run, resumed);
394	  const nextRunStatus = continueInterruptedDirectTurn
395	    ? "running"
396	    : args.run.mode === "direct" || args.run.mode === "commit"
397	    ? resolveDirectRunStatusFromWorkerOutput({
398	      workerStatus: resumed.state,
399	      renderedOutput: resumed.renderedOutput,
400	      currentText: resumed.currentText,
401	      lastText: resumed.lastText,
402	      outputEntries: resumed.outputEntries,
403	      pendingPermissions: resumed.pendingPermissions,
404	      pendingElicitations: resumed.pendingElicitations,
405	    })
406	    : "running";
407	
408	  if (resumed.outputEntries) {
409	    await writeWorkerOutputEntries(args.run.id, args.worker.id, resumed.outputEntries);
410	  }
411	  await reconcileRecoveredHumanInputEntries({
412	    runId: args.run.id,
413	    workerId: args.worker.id,
414	    activeElicitationRequestIds: (resumed.pendingElicitations ?? []).map((entry) => entry.requestId),
415	    activePermissionRequestIds: (resumed.pendingPermissions ?? []).map((entry) => entry.requestId),
416	    reason: "the runner restarted and the recovered runtime no longer owns this request",
417	  });
418	
419	  await db.update(workers).set({
420	    status: continueInterruptedDirectTurn ? "working" : resumed.state,
421	    currentText: resumed.currentText,
422	    lastText: resumed.lastText,
423	    bridgeSessionId: resumed.sessionId ?? (recreatedFromMissingSession ? null : sessionId),
424	    bridgeSessionMode: resumed.sessionMode ?? args.worker.bridgeSessionMode ?? null,
425	    updatedAt: new Date(),
426	  }).where(eq(workers.id, args.worker.id));
427	  emitNamedEvent({
428	    kind: recreatedFromMissingSession ? "worker.recreated" : "worker.reattached",
429	    runId: args.run.id,
430	    workerId: args.worker.id,
431	  });
432	  if (recreatedFromMissingSession) {
433	    await insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(args.run.id, args.worker.id, "worker_session_recreated", {
434	      summary: `Started a fresh runtime worker for ${args.worker.id} after its saved session was rejected.`,
435	      rejectedSessionId: sessionId,
436	      newSessionId: resumed.sessionId ?? null,
437	      reason: "recovery_resume_missing_agent",
438	    });
439	  }
440	  await db.update(runs).set({
441	    status: nextRunStatus,
442	    failedAt: null,
443	    lastError: null,
444	    updatedAt: new Date(),
445	  }).where(eq(runs.id, args.run.id));
446	  // The incident is "this worker's session was lost". Restoring it is done the
447	  // moment the resumed agent is persisted. Any continuation turn that follows is
448	  // ordinary work — the worker row already says `working` and the run says
449	  // `running`, which is what the normal progress UI is for. Holding the incident
450	  // open until that turn ends left the recovery banner claiming OmniHarness was
451	  // still restoring the session for as long as the agent kept working, which
452	  // reads as a hung backend.
453	  await markRecoveryIncidentResolved({
454	    incidentId: args.incidentId,
455	    runId: args.run.id,
456	    workerId: args.worker.id,
457	    summary: `Resumed ${args.worker.id} from saved session.`,
458	    details: {
459	      sessionId,
460	      workerState: continueInterruptedDirectTurn ? "working" : resumed.state,
461	      ...(continueInterruptedDirectTurn ? { continuationPending: true } : {}),
462	    },
463	  });
464	  if (continueInterruptedDirectTurn) {
465	    const continuation = runWorkerTurn(args.worker.id, () => finishRecoveredDirectTurn({
466	      run: args.run,
467	      worker: args.worker,
468	      resumed,
469	      incidentId: args.incidentId,
470	    }));
471	    trackConversationBackgroundTask(continuation, { runId: args.run.id }).catch((error) => {
472	      process.stderr.write(
473	        `[recovery] interrupted turn continuation failed for ${args.worker.id}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}\n`,
474	      );
475	    });
476	  }
477	  return { action: "resume_session" as const, runId: args.run.id, workerId: args.worker.id };
478	}
479	
480	async function restartFromCheckpoint(args: {
481	  run: typeof runs.$inferSelect;
482	  workerId?: string | null;
483	  state: RecoveryState;
484	  incidentId: string;
485	  preserveQueuedMessages: boolean;
486	}) {
487	  await markRecoveryIncidentRecovering({
488	    incidentId: args.incidentId,
489	    runId: args.run.id,
490	    workerId: args.workerId,
491	    decision: "restart_from_checkpoint",
492	    details: {
493	      queuedMessageId: args.state.queuedMessageId ?? null,
494	      preserveQueuedMessages: args.preserveQueuedMessages,
495	    },
496	  });
497	  await insertRecoveryExecutionEvent(args.run.id, args.workerId, "recovery_auto_restart_started", {
498	    summary: "Restarting implementation run from latest user checkpoint.",
499	    incidentId: args.incidentId,
500	    queuedMessageId: args.state.queuedMessageId ?? null,
501	  });
502	  await db.update(runs).set({
503	    status: "recovering",
504	    updatedAt: new Date(),
505	  }).where(eq(runs.id, args.run.id));
506	
507	  const result = await restartImplementationRunFromLatestCheckpoint({
508	    runId: args.run.id,
509	    workerId: args.workerId,
510	    preserveQueuedMessages: args.preserveQueuedMessages,
511	  });
512	  await markRecoveryIncidentResolved({
513	    incidentId: args.incidentId,
514	    runId: args.run.id,
515	    workerId: args.workerId,
516	    summary: "Restarted implementation run from latest user checkpoint.",
517	    details: result,
518	  });
519	  return { action: "restart_from_checkpoint" as const, ...result };
520	}
521	
522	export async function reconcileRunRecovery(args: {
523	  runId: string;
524	  liveAgents: RecoveryLiveAgentLike[];
525	  force?: boolean;
526	  source?: string;
527	}) {
528	  const { run, runWorkers, runMessages, runQueuedMessages } = await loadRunRecoveryInputs(args.runId);
529	  const state = classifyRunRecoveryState({
530	    run,
531	    workers: runWorkers,
532	    liveAgents: args.liveAgents,
533	    messages: runMessages,
534	    queuedMessages: runQueuedMessages,
535	  });
536	
537	  if (state.kind === "healthy" || state.kind === "recovering") {
538	    // A silent early return here left incidents from an earlier failure hanging
539	    // open long after the run went healthy again, which is what kept the recovery
540	    // banner on screen. `recovering` is genuinely still in flight, so only
541	    // `healthy` settles the leftovers.
542	    if (state.kind === "healthy") {
543	      const resolved = await resolveRecoveryIncidentsAfterHealthyTurn({
544	        runId: run.id,
545	        summary: "Run is healthy again; clearing leftover recovery incidents.",
546	        reason: "run_reconciled_healthy",
547	      });
548	      if (resolved > 0) {
549	        notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
550	      }
551	    }
552	    return { action: "none" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
553	  }
554	
555	  if (state.kind === "needs_recovery" && run.status === "needs_recovery" && !args.force) {
556	    return { action: "needs_user" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
557	  }
558	
559	  if (run.mode === "implementation" && normalizeRunStatus(run.status) === "awaiting_user") {
560	    await recordRecoveryPausedForUser({
561	      runId: run.id,
562	      workerId: state.workerId,
563	      state,
564	      source: args.source,
565	    });
566	    notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
567	    return { action: "none" as const, runId: run.id, recoveryState: state };
568	  }
569	
570	  const incident = await openRecoveryIncident({
571	    runId: run.id,
572	    workerId: state.workerId,
573	    queuedMessageId: state.queuedMessageId,
574	    kind: incidentKindForState(state),
575	    lastError: state.reason ?? null,
576	    details: {
577	      source: args.source ?? "reconciler",
578	      recoveryState: state.kind,
579	      recommendedAction: state.recommendedAction,
580	      reason: state.reason ?? null,
581	    },
582	  });
583	  const policy = await getRecoveryPolicy();
584	  const decision = decideRecoveryAction({
585	    runMode: run.mode,
586	    recoveryState: state,
587	    policy,
588	    autoAttemptCount: incident.autoAttemptCount,
589	    force: args.force,
590	  });
591	  if (decision.action === "needs_user") {
592	    await markNeedsUser({
```

```text
289	/**
290	 * Close any open `quota_exhausted` incidents for a run whose stored
291	 * `details.resumeAt` is in the past, and flip any `cred-exhausted`
292	 * worker rows on the same run to `stopped`. Called from the durable
293	 * quota-wake handler regardless of `runs.status`, so failover-success
294	 * runs (which never parked) still have their stale rows cleaned up.
295	 */
296	export async function clearResolvedQuotaIncidents(runId: string, options: { now?: Date } = {}) {
297	  const now = options.now ?? new Date();
298	  const incidents = await db.select()
299	    .from(recoveryIncidents)
300	    .where(and(
301	      eq(recoveryIncidents.runId, runId),
302	      eq(recoveryIncidents.kind, "quota_exhausted"),
303	      inArray(recoveryIncidents.status, [...OPEN_QUOTA_INCIDENT_STATUSES]),
304	    ));
305	
306	  let resolvedCount = 0;
307	  for (const incident of incidents) {
308	    const details = parseDetails(incident.details);
309	    const resumeAt = readResumeAt(details);
310	    if (!isResumeAtPast(resumeAt, now)) continue;
311	    await markRecoveryIncidentResolved({
312	      incidentId: incident.id,
313	      runId,
314	      workerId: incident.workerId ?? null,
315	      summary: "Quota reset window elapsed; incident auto-resolved.",
316	      details: {
317	        ...details,
318	        recoveryState: "quota_resolved",
319	        recommendedAction: "none",
320	        autoResolvedAt: now.toISOString(),
321	      },
322	    });
323	    resolvedCount += 1;
324	  }
325	
326	  if (resolvedCount > 0) {
327	    const credRows = await db.select()
328	      .from(workers)
329	      .where(and(
330	        eq(workers.runId, runId),
331	        eq(workers.status, "cred-exhausted"),

333	    for (const row of credRows) {
334	      await db.update(workers).set({

336	        updatedAt: now,
337	      }).where(eq(workers.id, row.id));
338	    }
339	  }
340	
341	  return { resolvedCount };
```

```text
18	function runOnChain<T>(
```
