## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T20:50:30.095Z

I need to implement a safety mechanism in the sync loop that clears stale recovery incidents once a worker shows genuine progress again. The key is preventing flapping by only resolving incidents that were detected before the worker actually started working, not ones that just opened moments ago.

For `quota_exhausted` incidents, if the agent is actively streaming, the quota must be fine, so those can be cleared. But `worker_lost` or `session_missing` incidents marked as `needs_user` are definitely stale if the agent is live and working. The safest condition is to only resolve unsettled incidents when the live agent exists and is actively producing output—that's the clearest signal the worker has recovered.

The tricky part is using the live agent's state from the bridge, not the potentially stale DB row. And to avoid clearing a freshly opened quota incident while the agent transiently reports working, I should add a grace period—either require the incident to be at least 30 seconds old, or check that there's been output produced after the incident was detected.

I can use `workers.active_work_started_at` as the cutoff—if it's reliably set at turn start, I can resolve incidents that predate that timestamp.

2	 * Watchdog for direct-mode workers that get stuck in `status='working'`

4	 *
5	 * Root cause this addresses: the ACP roundtrip for a prompt can silently
6	 * drop — gemini/codex/claude receives "continue" but never produces a
7	 * response, the agent runtime never notices, and the worker sits at
8	 * state='working' indefinitely. Nothing in the existing supervisor
9	 * watchdog checks for this because it only inspects implementation
10	 * runs.
11	 *
12	 * Recovery contract: if a direct worker is working but has produced no
13	 * stream entries for OMNIHARNESS_WORKER_STUCK_TIMEOUT_MS (default 5
14	 * minutes), cancel the hung agent, spawn a fresh one via the same
15	 * resume-or-recreate primitive that on-send recovery uses, and
16	 * re-deliver the last user message that has no follow-up response. The
17	 * user sees activity resume on its own.
18	 */

35

37	const DIRECT_MODE_NAMES = ["direct"];

40	function readPositiveIntegerEnv(name: string, fallback: number): number {
41	  const raw = process.env[name];

9	const LEASE_KEY_PREFIX = "SUPERVISOR_WAKE_LEASE:";
10	
11	type SupervisorWakeLease = {
12	  leaseId: string;
13	  expiresAt: number;
14	};
15	
16	function leaseKey(runId: string) {
17	  return `${LEASE_KEY_PREFIX}${runId}`;
18	}
19	
20	function parseLease(value: string): SupervisorWakeLease | null {
21	  try {
22	    const parsed = JSON.parse(value) as Partial<SupervisorWakeLease>;
23	    return typeof parsed.leaseId === "string" && typeof parsed.expiresAt === "number"
24	      ? { leaseId: parsed.leaseId, expiresAt: parsed.expiresAt }
25	      : null;
26	  } catch {
27	    return null;
28	  }
29	}
30	
31	export async function acquireSupervisorWakeLease(runId: string, now = Date.now()) {
32	  const key = leaseKey(runId);
33	  const existing = await db.select().from(settings).where(eq(settings.key, key)).get();
34	  const existingLease = existing ? parseLease(existing.value) : null;
35	  if (existingLease && existingLease.expiresAt > now) {
36	    emitNamedEvent({ kind: "supervisor.wake_lease_blocked", runId, reason: "active_lease" });
37	    return null;
38	  }
39	
40	  const lease: SupervisorWakeLease = {
41	    leaseId: randomUUID(),
42	    expiresAt: now + LEASE_TTL_MS,
43	  };
44	  const value = JSON.stringify(lease);
45	
46	  if (!existing) {
47	    try {
48	      await withSqliteBusyRetry(() => db.insert(settings).values({ key, value, updatedAt: new Date(now) }));
49	      emitNamedEvent({ kind: "supervisor.wake_lease_acquired", runId, source: "insert" });
50	      return lease.leaseId;
51	    } catch {
52	      emitNamedEvent({ kind: "supervisor.wake_lease_blocked", runId, reason: "insert_conflict" });
53	      return null;
54	    }
55	  }
56	
57	  const replaceSource = existingLease ? "replace_expired" : "replace_malformed";
58	  await withSqliteBusyRetry(() => db.update(settings)
59	    .set({ value, updatedAt: new Date(now) })
60	    .where(and(eq(settings.key, key), eq(settings.value, existing.value))));
61	
62	  const claimed = await db.select().from(settings).where(eq(settings.key, key)).get();
63	  if (claimed?.value === value) {
64	    emitNamedEvent({ kind: "supervisor.wake_lease_acquired", runId, source: replaceSource });
65	    return lease.leaseId;
66	  }
67	  emitNamedEvent({ kind: "supervisor.wake_lease_blocked", runId, reason: "claim_race" });
68	  return null;

76	    return;

78	
79	  const existingLease = existing ? parseLease(existing.value) : null;

3	export function recoveryTone(state: RunRecoveryState | null | undefined) {
4	  if (!state) return "muted" as const;
5	  if (state.status === "failed") return "error" as const;
6	  if (state.status === "needs_user" || state.kind === "needs_recovery") return "warning" as const;
7	  if (state.status === "recovering") return "active" as const;
8	  return "warning" as const;
9	}
10	
11	export function recoveryTitleKey(state: RunRecoveryState | null | undefined) {
12	  if (!state) return "recovery.notice.title.default";
13	  if (state.kind === "quota_waiting") return "recovery.notice.title.quotaWaiting";
14	  if (state.status === "recovering") return "recovery.notice.title.recovering";
15	  if (state.status === "failed") return "recovery.notice.title.failed";
16	  if (state.kind === "queue_blocked") return "recovery.notice.title.queueBlocked";
17	  if (state.kind === "lost_worker_resumable") return "recovery.notice.title.workerDisconnected";
18	  if (state.kind === "lost_worker_rerunnable") return "recovery.notice.title.workerDisconnected";
19	  return "recovery.notice.title.needsRecovery";
20	}
21	
22	export function recoveryDescriptionKey(state: RunRecoveryState | null | undefined) {

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-05T20:51:07.744Z

So `activeWorkStartedAt` tracks when a worker began their current working period—it's set when status transitions into `working` and cleared when they stop. This means I can identify stale incidents by checking if the incident was detected before the worker started their current work session, which would indicate the incident is outdated and should be resolved.

I'm creating a reusable function in the recovery incidents module that takes a worker's run ID and worker ID, then queries for any incidents where `detectedAt` is earlier than `activeWorkStartedAt`. These are incidents that predate the current working period, so they're disproved by the fact that the worker is actively running now. The function will be called from the sync loop whenever a worker transitions into the working state, clearing out these stale bookkeeping entries without affecting incidents that occurred during the current session.

Writing the recovery function... I'm considering where to trigger this sweep in sync.ts. Doing it on every work status update would add a query per pass, which is expensive since sync runs frequently. A better approach is to only run the sweep when the worker transitions into the working state — that's a rare event and exactly when we need it. So I'd check if the worker's status is changing to 'working', and at that point we have the activeWorkStartedAt from the database update. Now I need to implement the recovery incident sweep function in recovery-incidents.ts and wire it up in sync.ts to run when the worker transitions to working. Let me check the existing code structure and imports to keep things consistent.

## Claude subagent agent-a3e287d6d62e671e7: Claude · 2026-08-05T20:52:24.123Z

````text
Confirmed: `askAgent` has no timeout — only an ambient abort signal that recovery paths never publish (they call it outside `runWorkerTurn`). My audit is complete.

## Findings, worst first

### 1. HIGH — `quota/worker-resume.ts`: `cred-exhausted` worker status never cleared on the resume path (the *un-fixed half* of confirmed instance #2)

`src/server/quota/worker-resume.ts:190-197` and `:116-122`

The quota block sets `workers.status = "cred-exhausted"` (`src/server/quota/recovery.ts:121-124`). On resume, the row is rewritten twice — first with `resumedWorker.state` (line 190), then with `response.state` after `await askAgent` (line 116). But **`markRecoveryIncidentResolved` at line 209 is the only thing that runs after `await promptResumedQuotaWorker(...)` at line 199**, and there is a second consumer of `cred-exhausted` that this path never reaches: `clearResolvedQuotaIncidents` (`src/server/quota/type-blocking.ts:326-339`) is the *only* code that sweeps `cred-exhausted` → `stopped`, and `wake.ts:348` only calls it in the `run.status !== "quota_waiting"` branch — i.e. **explicitly not** on the `resumeQuotaExhaustedWorkers` path (`src/server/supervisor/wake.ts:343-349`, comment: *"which therefore wouldn't be touched by the resumeQuotaExhaustedWorkers path below"*).

Consequence beyond the banner: `blockedWorkerTypesForRun` treats any `cred-exhausted` row as a live block (`type-blocking.ts:105-112`, `:190-196`). So while the resumed worker's turn runs, **the whole worker type stays marked as quota-blocked for spawn selection**, and if `askAgent` never returns, it stays blocked forever. Severity high: no timeout, no sweep on this path.

State that goes stale: `recoveryIncidents.status='open'` + worker type blocklist. User sees: "Waiting for quota reset" banner (`recovery-utils.ts:13` → `recovery.notice.title.quotaWaiting`) while the worker is demonstrably streaming output, and failover refuses to pick that type.

### 2. HIGH — `supervisor/worker-failover.ts:392` → incident resolved at `:421`, run status reset at `:439`

```
392:      const response = await bridge.askAgent(newWorkerId, seed);
...
421:      await markRecoveryIncidentResolved({ incidentId: block.incidentId, ... failover_pending: false, ...});
439:      await db.update(runs).set({ status: "running", failedAt: null, lastError: null, ...});
```

The failover handoff seed is a **full worker turn** on a brand-new worker (a seeded continuation, so typically long). Everything that clears the user-visible failure state — the `quota_exhausted` incident, `failover_pending: false`, and the run's `status`/`failedAt`/`lastError` reset — is sequenced after it.

State that goes stale: the `quota_exhausted` incident stays `open`/`needs_user`, and `runs.status` stays whatever the quota handler parked it at (`quota_waiting` per `quota/recovery.ts:200-205`, or `needs_recovery` per `:175-179`). User sees: the quota/recovery banner, plus `runs.lastError` still rendered. Why the clear may not run: `askAgent` (`bridge-client/index.ts:646`) has no timeout; the ambient abort signal at `:654` comes from `currentWorkerTurnSignal()`, and **`attemptWorkerFailover` is not wrapped in `runWorkerTurn`** (called from `supervisor/index.ts:1507` and `:1614`, both outside any `runWorkerTurn`), so the signal is `undefined` and there is nothing to abort it. Severity high: hangs indefinitely, and the same catch-block path at `:473` only fires on throw.

Note this is exactly the shape the reconciler already fixed for itself (`recovery-reconciler.ts:446-463` comment: *"Holding the incident open until that turn ends left the recovery banner claiming OmniHarness was still restoring the session for as long as the agent kept working, which reads as a hung backend."*).

### 3. HIGH (category b) — `supervisor/wake.ts:311` and `:358`: unbounded worker turn inside the held supervisor wake lease

```
263:  const leaseId = await acquireSupervisorWakeLease(runId);
...
311:        const quotaResumeResult = await resumeQuotaExhaustedWorkers({ run });
...
333:      await releaseSupervisorWakeLease(runId, leaseId);
...
358:      const quotaResumeResult = await resumeQuotaExhaustedWorkers({ run });
```

`resumeQuotaExhaustedWorkers` awaits `askAgent` per worker (`worker-resume.ts:94`), inside a `for` loop over all incidents (`:154`), while holding the run's exclusive wake lease. The lease is a serialized chain in the sense the task asks about: any concurrent `executeSupervisorWake` for the same run bails with `reason: "lease_blocked"` (`wake.ts:273-275`) and reschedules.

The lease does have a bound — `LEASE_TTL_MS = 15 * 60_000` (`supervisor/lease.ts:8`) — so a wedged turn parks the run's supervisor for **up to 15 minutes**, not forever. But note the run status was already flipped to `running` at `wake.ts:304-309` / `:351-356` *before* the resume, so during that window the UI shows a running run with a supervisor that is making no progress. Severity high but self-limiting via the TTL.

### 4. MEDIUM-HIGH — `runs/recovery.ts:901`: `resolveOpenRecoveryIncidentsForRun` sequenced after `await askAgent` at `:819-820`

```
819:      ? await askAgent(worker.id, retryPrompt, retryImages)
820:      : await askAgent(worker.id, retryPrompt);
...
901:  await resolveOpenRecoveryIncidentsForRun(run.id, worker.id, `Recovered ${worker.id}.`);
```

This is the **manual** recovery path (user clicks resume/retry). The session is already restored and persisted much earlier — `workers.status='working'` at `:777-782` and `runs.status='running', failedAt:null, lastError:null` at `:792-797`. So the run and worker already read as healthy, but every incident (`open`, `recovering`, `needs_user`, **and `failed`** — see `:985`) stays unresolved until the retry turn finishes.

State that goes stale: `recoveryIncidents` rows in all four unsettled statuses. User sees: the recovery banner still up, with tone `error` for `failed` or `warning` for `needs_user` (`recovery-utils.ts:5-6`), on a run that has already gone back to `running`. Contradictory state: green run, red recovery banner. Why the clear may not run: no timeout on `askAgent`; this call is **not** inside `runWorkerTurn`, so no ambient abort signal. The early-returns at `:811` (worker already active) and `:847` (agent busy) also skip line 901 entirely, leaving incidents unresolved permanently on those two branches. Severity: high user-visible wrongness, but the incident does get swept later if `reconcileRunRecovery` runs and classifies the run `healthy` (`recovery-reconciler.ts:542-551`).

### 5. MEDIUM — `workers/stuck-worker-reaper.ts:300-303`: `status='stuck'` written before an unbounded `await askAgent` at `:338`

```
300:        await db.update(workers).set({ status: "stuck", updatedAt: new Date() })
303:          .where(eq(workers.id, worker.id));
304:        notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
...
338:            const response = await askAgent(worker.id, content);
342:            await persistRedeliveredTurnResult({ worker, responseText: response.response ?? null });
```

The reaper deliberately publishes `stuck` to the UI (`notifyEventStreamSubscribers()` at 304), then redelivers the prompt and only clears the status inside `persistRedeliveredTurnResult` at `:342` (which writes `snapshot?.state ?? "idle"` at `:125-128`) — *after* the whole redelivered turn.

State that goes stale: `workers.status='stuck'`. User sees: `supervisor.activity.worker.stuck` with an attention flag (`src/interface/home/supervisor-activity.ts:136-140`), and `useHomeViewModel.ts:579` flips the conversation into a stuck-warning state. So the worker is flagged as stuck to the user for the entire duration of the very turn that is un-sticking it.

Mitigation that keeps this from being top-tier: the header comment at `:101-107` shows this path was already hardened once for the *infinite re-reap loop*, the `catch` at `:360` writes `status='error'`, and the reaper is idempotent-ish across sweeps (`STUCK_CANDIDATE_STATUSES` at `:38` is `{working, starting}`, so a `stuck` row is skipped by the next sweep rather than re-reaped). Severity medium: wrong UI state for the length of a turn, but bounded by the turn and not self-amplifying.

### 6. LOW-MEDIUM (category c) — `quota/recovery.ts:121-124`: `cred-exhausted` written on failure, cleared only by one narrow sweep

`workers.status='cred-exhausted'` is set unconditionally when a quota block is recorded. The **only** code that clears it is `clearResolvedQuotaIncidents` (`type-blocking.ts:326-339`), which:
- requires at least one incident to actually resolve in that same call (`if (resolvedCount > 0)` at `:326`), and
- is only invoked from `wake.ts:348`, gated on `dueDurableWake?.reason === "quota_wait" && run.status !== "quota_waiting"`.

So for a run that *did* park at `quota_waiting` (the normal case, `quota/recovery.ts:200-205`), the sweep never runs — that path goes through `resumeQuotaExhaustedWorkers` instead, which never touches `cred-exhausted` (see finding 1). If the durable wake row is lost (`wake-schedule.ts:167-169` deletes wakes for terminal/archived runs; `claimDueDurableSupervisorWake` at `:137-152` deletes on claim), nothing ever clears the row. Severity low-medium: mostly invisible to the user, but it silently keeps a worker type on the spawn blocklist.

---

## Notable non-findings (checked, correctly handled)

- `runs/recovery-reconciler.ts` — the canonical correct pattern. Incident resolved at `:453` **before** the continuation turn, which is dispatched as a background task at `:465-475`. Explicit comment at `:446-452`. Also `finishRecoveredDirectTurn` only *reopens* on failure (`:177`), never gates the clear.
- `conversations/queued-message-interrupt.ts` — `delivering` is fully hardened: `releaseSupersededRow` at `:364-388` explicitly exists because *"Bailing out used to just `return`, which left the row in `delivering` forever"*, plus `isStillCurrent` re-checks at `:405`, `:433`, `:449`, `:462`, and a catch at `:493`. Delivery is backgrounded at `:290-305`.
- `conversations/queued-messages.ts:1300-1439` — the drain wraps the turn in `runWorkerTurn` (so `askAgent` picks up the abort signal via `currentWorkerTurnSignal()`) and has a full try/catch that returns the row to `pending`/`failed` at `:1399` and `:1408`. `reclaimOrphanedDeliveringMessages` at `:472-497` is a real boot-time reconciliation sweep.
- `runtime/http/routes/runs.ts:256-276` — `settleRunRecoveryAfterUserStop` has no worker turn before it.
- `supervisor/index.ts:1487` / `:1595` — awaits `askAgent` but does not gate any recovery/status *clear* behind it; the worker row is updated with `response.state` and failures go through `deferBusyWorkerPrompt` / quota handlers.

## Recommended fix shape

Findings 1, 2 and 4 all resolve the same way the reconciler already does it: move the incident resolution / status reset to **before** the turn (the session is restored and persisted at that point — that is the incident), and dispatch the continuation turn via `trackConversationBackgroundTask(runWorkerTurn(...))`. Wrapping in `runWorkerTurn` additionally gives these paths the ambient abort signal they currently lack, which is what makes them unbounded today. Finding 3 wants the resume moved out from under the lease, or the lease released before the prompt. Findings 1 and 6 want `cred-exhausted` cleared on the `resumeQuotaExhaustedWorkers` path (or `clearResolvedQuotaIncidents` called unconditionally there).

HIGH — `supervisor/worker-failover.ts:392` → incident resolved at `:421`, run status reset at `:439`\n\n```\n392:      const response = await bridge.askAgent(newWorkerId, seed);\n...\n421:      await markRecoveryIncidentResolved({ incidentId: block.incidentId, ... failover_pending: false, ...});\n439:      await db.update(runs).set({ status: \"running\", failedAt: null, lastError: null, ...});\n```\n\nThe failover handoff seed is a **full worker turn** on a brand-new worker (a seeded continuation, so typically long). The lease is a serialized chain in the sense the task asks about: any concurrent `executeSupervisorWake` for the same run bails with `reason: \"lease_blocked\"` (`wake.ts:273-275`) and reschedules.\n\nThe lease does have a bound — `LEASE_TTL_MS = 15 * 60_000` (`supervisor/lease.ts:8`) — so a wedged turn parks the run's supervisor for **up to 15 minutes**, not forever. Severity medium: wrong UI state for the length of a turn, but bounded by the turn and not self-amplifying.\n\n### 6. LOW-MEDIUM (category c) — `quota/recovery.ts:121-124`: `cred-exhausted` written on failure, cleared only by one narrow sweep\n\n`workers.status='cred-exhausted'` is set unconditionally when a quota block is recorded. MEDIUM-HIGH — `runs/recovery.ts:901`: `resolveOpenRecoveryIncidentsForRun` sequenced after `await askAgent` at `:819-820`\n\n```\n819:      ? await askAgent(worker.id, retryPrompt, retryImages)\n820:      : await askAgent(worker.id, retryPrompt);\n...\n901:  await resolveOpenRecoveryIncidentsForRun(run.id, worker.id, `Recovered ${worker.id}.`);\n```\n\nThis is the **manual** recovery path (user clicks resume/retry). The session is already restored and persisted much earlier — `workers.status='working'` at `:777-782` and `runs.status='running', failedAt:null, lastError:null` at `:792-797`. So the run and worker already read as healthy, but every incident (`open`, `recovering`, `needs_user`, **and `failed`** — see `:985`) stays unresolved until the retry turn finishes.\n\nState that goes stale: `recoveryIncidents` rows in all four unsettled statuses. User sees: the recovery banner still up, with tone `error` for `failed` or `warning` for `needs_user` (`recovery-utils.ts:5-6`), on a run that has already gone back to `running`. Contradictory state: green run, red recovery banner. Why the clear may not run: no timeout on `askAgent`; this call is **not** inside `runWorkerTurn`, so no ambient abort signal. The early-returns at `:811` (worker already active) and `:847` (agent busy) also skip line 901 entirely, leaving incidents unresolved permanently on those two branches. Severity: high user-visible wrongness, but the incident does get swept later if `reconcileRunRecovery` runs and classifies the run `healthy` (`recovery-reconciler.ts:542-551`).\n\n### 5. MEDIUM — `workers/stuck-worker-reaper.ts:300-303`: `status='stuck'` written before an unbounded `await askAgent` at `:338`\n\n```\n300:        await db.update(workers).set({ status: \"stuck\", updatedAt: new Date() })\n303:          .where(eq(workers.id, worker.id));\n304:        notifyEventStreamSubscribers();\n...\n338:            const response = await askAgent(worker.id, content);\n342:            await persistRedeliveredTurnResult({ worker, responseText: response.response ?? null });\n```\n\nThe reaper deliberately publishes `stuck` to the UI (`notifyEventStreamSubscribers()` at 304), then redelivers the prompt and only clears the status inside `persistRedeliveredTurnResult` at `:342` (which writes `snapshot?.state ?? \"idle\"` at `:125-128`) — *after* the whole redelivered turn.\n\nState that goes stale: `workers.status='stuck'`. User sees: `supervisor.activity.worker.stuck` with an attention flag (`src/interface/home/supervisor-activity.ts:136-140`), and `useHomeViewModel.ts:579` flips the conversation into a stuck-warning state. So the worker is flagged as stuck to the user for the entire duration of the very turn that is un-sticking it.\n\nMitigation that keeps this from being top-tier: the header comment at `:101-107` shows this path was already hardened once for the *infinite re-reap loop*, the `catch` at `:360` writes `status='error'`, and the reaper is idempotent-ish across sweeps (`STUCK_CANDIDATE_STATUSES` at `:38` is `{working, starting}`, so a `stuck` row is skipped by the next sweep rather than re-reaped). Severity medium: wrong UI state for the length of a turn, but bounded by the turn and not self-amplifying.\n\n### 6. LOW-MEDIUM (category c) — `quota/recovery.ts:121-124`: `cred-exhausted` written on failure, cleared only by one narrow sweep\n\n`workers.status='cred-exhausted'` is set unconditionally when a quota block is recorded. The **only** code that clears it is `clearResolvedQuotaIncidents` (`type-blocking.ts:326-339`), which:\n- requires at least one incident to actually resolve in that same call (`if (resolvedCount &gt; 0)` at `:326`), and\n- is only invoked from `wake.ts:348`, gated on `dueDurableWake?.reason === \"quota_wait\" &amp;&amp; run.status !== \"quota_waiting\"`.\n\nSo for a run that *did* park at `quota_waiting` (the normal case, `quota/recovery.ts:200-205`), the sweep never runs — that path goes through `resumeQuotaExhaustedWorkers` instead, which never touches `cred-exhausted` (see finding 1). If the durable wake row is lost (`wake-schedule.ts:167-169` deletes wakes for terminal/archived runs; `claimDueDurableSupervisorWake` at `:137-152` deletes on claim), nothing ever clears the row. Severity low-medium: mostly invisible to the user, but it silently keeps a worker type on the spawn blocklist.\n\n---\n\n## Notable non-findings (checked, correctly handled)\n\n- `runs/recovery-reconciler.ts` — the canonical correct pattern. Incident resolved at `:453` **before** the continuation turn, which is dispatched as a background task at `:465-475`. Explicit comment at `:446-452`. Also `finishRecoveredDirectTurn` only *reopens* on failure (`:177`), never gates the clear.\n- `conversations/queued-message-interrupt.ts` — `delivering` is fully hardened: `releaseSupersededRow` at `:364-388` explicitly exists because *\"Bailing out used to just `return`, which left the row in `delivering` forever\"*, plus `isStillCurrent` re-checks at `:405`, `:433`, `:449`, `:462`, and a catch at `:493`. Delivery is backgrounded at `:290-305`.\n- `conversations/queued-messages.ts:1300-1439` — the drain wraps the turn in `runWorkerTurn` (so `askAgent` picks up the abort signal via `currentWorkerTurnSignal()`) and has a full try/catch that returns the row to `pending`/`failed` at `:1399` and `:1408`. `reclaimOrphanedDeliveringMessages` at `:472-497` is a real boot-time reconciliation sweep.\n- `runtime/http/routes/runs.ts:256-276` — `settleRunRecoveryAfterUserStop` has no worker turn before it.\n- `supervisor/index.ts:1487` / `:1595` — awaits `askAgent` but does not gate any recovery/status *clear* behind it; the worker row is updated with `response.state` and failures go through `deferBusyWorkerPrompt` / quota handlers.\n\n## Recommended fix shape\n\nFindings 1, 2 and 4 all resolve the same way the reconciler already does it: move the incident resolution / status reset to **before** the turn (the session is restored and persisted at that point — that is the incident), and dispatch the continuation turn via `trackConversationBackgroundTask(runWorkerTurn(...))`. Wrapping in `runWorkerTurn` additionally gives these paths the ambient abort signal they currently lack, which is what makes them unbounded today. Finding 3 wants the resume moved out from under the lease, or the lease released before the prompt. Findings 1 and 6 want `cred-exhausted` cleared on the `resumeQuotaExhaustedWorkers` path (or `clearResolvedQuotaIncidents` called unconditionally there).</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>122344</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>39</tool_uses><duration_ms>156978</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>",

Looking at the event timeline from the logs, I'm seeing a pattern of recovery and session management issues—automatic recovery was disabled, the worker resumed from a saved session, and then auto-commit kept getting skipped because recovery was still in progress and blocking the queue.

The incident was first detected at 17:55:24 but wasn't re-marked as needing user intervention until 22:54:14, which is when the recovery_needs_user event fired. The worker then successfully resumed and completed its work within 27 seconds (22:54:15 to 22:54:42), but the incident remained open during that entire window, only resolving at turn completion.

The real issue here is that the user saw the "Queued message blocked / Automatic recovery is disabled" banner while the session was actually functioning fine—the worker was actively processing and the recovery completed successfully, but the incident status wasn't reflecting that reality in real time.

My new sweep logic would have caught this immediately: once the worker transitioned to working status at 22:54:15, the sweep would have fired and resolved the incident right then, rather than waiting until 22:54:42. But the deeper question is what was happening during those 5 hours between initial detection and the re-marking at 22:54:14—was the worker actually working during that stretch, and if so, why didn't the sweep clear it then?

I need to look at the recovery policy logic to understand why direct/omni conversation modes have automatic recovery disabled, which is causing queue_blocked incidents to get stuck in needs_user status until a turn completes, even though the system can self-heal.

## Claude · 2026-08-05T20:57:25.757Z

Same family, third instance — and this one exposes a real gap in the sweep I just added. Not flakiness on your side.

## What happened on `36e4c3f00a7d`

Everything below landed in a **single second**, 17:55:24:

```
queued_message_interrupt_failed
queued_message_recovery_blocked
recovery_incident_opened        ← queue_blocked
recovery_needs_user             ← "Automatic recovery is disabled for this conversation mode."
worker_session_resumed          ← the session came back, successfully
```

Then **nothing for five hours**. The incident finally cleared at 22:54:42, with:

```json
{"reason":"worker_turn_succeeded","resolvedByHealthyTurn":true,"previousStatus":"needs_user"}
```

So the session recovered *one second after* the incident opened, and the banner claimed it was blocked for the next five hours. The "Automatic recovery is disabled for this conversation mode" text is `recovery-policy.ts:172` — auto-recovery is off for direct runs, so the incident is parked at `needs_user` by design. The design flaw is that nothing ever un-parks it except a completed turn.

## Root cause — same shape, worse

The only thing in the system that clears recovery state is a *finished turn*. A **successful session resume — the actual proof of recovery — clears nothing.**

In `src/server/runs/recovery.ts`, `resolveOpenRecoveryIncidentsForRun` is at line 901, behind the retry ask at 818-820. Worse, two early returns skip it entirely:

```
811:      return { runId: run.id };   // "worker is already active"
847:      return { runId: run.id };   // "worker is already busy"
```

On those branches the incident is never resolved at all — it just waits for some future turn. That's your five hours.

## I have to flag a gap in my own fix

The sweep I added fires on the transition **into `working`**. Here the worker resumed and sat **idle**, waiting for you. No transition, no sweep. **My change would not have caught this one.** The fence I chose is too narrow — it should key off *proof of health* (a successful resume), not just the start of work.

## Where things stand

- **Quota fix** (`63b477920b47`) — applied, with 2 regression tests that fail without it and pass with it.
- **General sweep** — added with 2 tests, but see the gap above.
- **Item 2, clearing that live banner** — turned out unnecessary. It self-cleared at 22:39:37 when its turn ended. I did not touch your live data.
- **The audit** — found 6 instances of this class. This bug is finding #4. Another HIGH one is still unfixed: `supervisor/worker-failover.ts:392`, where the incident resolve *and* the `runs.status`/`lastError` reset all sit behind a full seeded turn on a brand-new worker, with no abort signal.
- **Loose end I owe you:** 2 tests fail only under the full parallel suite and pass in isolation. I have not yet confirmed whether that's pre-existing or mine.

## Proposed fix

Resolve stale recovery state at the point of **successful session resume** — the `worker_session_resumed` hook — rather than at turn completion, and widen the sweep's fence from "started working" to "observed healthy". Plus move `resolveOpenRecoveryIncidentsForRun` ahead of the retry ask so the early returns can't skip it, and apply the same reordering to `worker-failover.ts`.

That covers findings 1, 2 and 4 together and is what would have prevented all three sessions you've hit.

Want me to go ahead with that? And should I chase the 2 suite-only test failures first, or after?

The user mentioned losing the "outside semi circle lines," so I'm comparing the asset file against the glyph implementation. The asset has arcs spanning specific coordinates plus circles and a horizontal line, while the glyph also has arcs and vertical bars. But here's the key insight: the SVG asset files have fixed dimensions (64×64) with no viewBox attribute, which means they could be getting cropped when rendered in certain contexts like the app header or favicon.

If the logo is displayed at a different size or scaled by the browser, a no-viewBox SVG won't scale its content properly—it just clips to the viewport. So rendering at 32px would crop to the top-left 32×32 region, cutting off the right node and parts of the arcs. That matches the "cropped too close" description. Now I need to verify whether these logo assets are actually being used anywhere in the codebase, checking the manifest, electron config, and mobile files to confirm this hypothesis.

## Claude · 2026-08-05T21:12:24.183Z

## The cause

`src/components/OmniHarnessMark.tsx`:

```jsx
<span className="... overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-[#fffdf8] p-[3px] ...">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 64 64" className="h-full w-full scale-[1.75]">
```

A clipping round container plus a 1.75× zoom on the SVG inside it. The arcs are the outermost geometry, so they're the first thing the clip eats.

The numbers work out exactly:

- At 1.75×, the visible slice of the viewBox is `64 / 1.75 ≈ 36.6` units centred on (32,32) — so only **x,y ∈ [13.7, 50.3]** survives.
- The arcs run from x=6.5 to x=57.5 and peak at y≈4.1 and y≈59.9. **Every extreme of both arcs sits outside that window.** The arc only re-enters the window right at the diagonal corners (≈13.7, 13.7) — and `rounded-full` clips the corners too.
- The H is at x 23–41, y 24–40 — comfortably inside. So it's the only thing left.

That's precisely your symptom: ring gone, H intact.

I confirmed the utility really is active in the CSS the runner is serving (my first grep missed it because CSS escapes the brackets):

```
dist/interface/assets/main-R2wYyISa.css:  .scale-\[1\.75\]{scale:1.75}
```

And the artwork is untouched — the component still has both arcs, the same paths as the PNG app icon:

```
<path d="M6.5 28A25.8 25.8 0 0 1 57.5 28" />
<path d="M57.5 36A25.8 25.8 0 0 1 6.5 36" />
```

## On the timing

Your Vite hunch doesn't hold up. `scale-[1.75]` and `overflow-hidden rounded-full` were added **together in one commit**, `2dd762b` on **2026-05-20** — eleven weeks before the Vite split (`e90cabf`, Jul 31). The sidebar has rendered this component since `e244894` on 2026-05-10. Tailwind was already v4 on both sides of the migration, so the utility compiled the same way before and after.

The header instance is worse, incidentally: `HomeHeader.tsx:347` passes `p-1`, which `cn` merges over the base `p-[3px]`, shrinking the inner box further.

For the record on your first question: no image, SVG, or component file is modified in the working tree, and my changes this session were confined to `src/server/**` and tests.
